title: (Palma) C21
description: El libro que contiene las misas propias del santoral, desde enero hasta junio, es un cantoral de grandes dimensiones, con cubiertas de madera semiforradas en cuero (729 × 499 mm), reforzadas con remaches lisos y cintas de latón. Consta de 113 folios de pergamino (689 × 477 mm) y un último folio adherido al interior de la contraportada. Se identifican varias manos; aunque todas mantienen una disposición de cinco líneas por columna, presentan diferencias notables en la ornamentación y el trazado:  1. Folios de 689 × 477 mm con caja de escritura de 524 × 316 mm. Los márgenes están ornamentados con un rectángulo de 23 mm de ancho que alterna rombos verdes y blancos decorados con doble línea transversal roja o con flores naranjas de cinco pétalos invertidas (en el margen izquierdo) y en posición normal (en el derecho). Las iniciales de inicio de festividad presentan trazos gruesos y formas geométricas (177 × 95 mm). Las capitulares de inicio de canto, de 95 × 35 mm, se ejecutan con doble línea negra y decoración de puntos romboides, o bien sin ornamentos, a una sola línea roja. Las iniciales de versículo siguen el mismo diseño, aunque de menor tamaño (75 × 30 mm o 55 × 20 mm), salvo en la secuencia del folio 3v, donde miden aproximadamente 35 × 22 mm y son de color rojo. Corresponde a los folios 1 al 6.  2. Folios de 689 × 477 mm con caja de escritura de 524 × 316 mm y margen rectangular de doble línea negra (605 × 371 mm), que forma compartimentos vacíos de unos 10 mm de ancho. Las iniciales de festividad alcanzan hasta 170 × 150 mm, en colores rojo, verde y amarillo, con decoración de trenzas gruesas de inspiración celta. Destaca la ilustración de San Juan Bautista en el folio 101. Las iniciales de canto y versículo siguen el mismo diseño que el tipo 1. Abarca los folios 7 al 12, 14 al 36, 68 al 77 y 98 al 113. Cabe señalar que el folio 20v presenta 15 líneas y el 21r siete líneas de pentagrama rojo de 25 mm de altura, en contraste con los 75 mm habituales.  3. Folios de 594 × 390 mm con caja de escritura de 524 × 316 mm. Las iniciales de canto y versículo siguen el modelo del tipo 1 (aprox. 95 × 40 mm), salvo los versos de la secuencia del folio 53v, de menor tamaño. Corresponde a los folios 51 al 60.  4. Resto de folios de varias manos, sin decoraciones marginales y en pergamino de mayor grosor. Algunos presentan decoraciones florales en las iniciales de festividades y cantos; otros siguen el estilo descrito en el tipo 2.     Destaca en el folio 41 un escudo, posiblemente de la familia  Fuster Togores, de grandes dimensiones (538 × 315 mm),  guillotinado en su parte superior. El escudo se divide en dos mitades: a la izquierda, sobre fondo azul, una estrella de ocho puntas; a la derecha, sobre fondo rojo, un grifo de alas cortas de color púrpura. Todo el conjunto está coronado por un casco de caballero y flanqueado por dos figuras semejantes a fuentes, con cabezas animales no identificadas que vierten agua.           El estado de conservación es heterogéneo, aunque en general el manuscrito presenta problemas de humedad, especialmente visibles en la alteración de los colores y en las marcas de uso. La calidad del pergamino también es desigual: los tipos 1 y 2 corresponden a ejemplares de mejor factura y acabado. Se identifican dos sistemas de foliación: una original y otra posterior, que sigue el orden actual de la encuadernación.     Presenta secuencias con notación mensural en los folios 3v y 53v.

title: (Palma) C23
description: El libro que contiene las misas del común de los Apóstoles y el común de los Mártires es un cantoral de grandes dimensiones, con cubiertas de madera semiforradas en cuero de 710 x 460 mm reforzadas con remaches decorados y cintas de latón, y un total de 116 folios de pergamino de 670 x 450 mm. Cada folio contiene cinco líneas escritas a una columna en una caja de escritura de 580x290 mm. Márgenes marcados con doble línea negra 700 x 500 mm. La notación es cuadrada sobre pentagramas rojo de 60 mm de alto. El tipo de escritura es gótico, de 18mm de alto las minúsculas, y de 185 x 180 las capitales de principio de oficio, profusamente decoradas en rojo, azul y papel de oro con motivos geométricos, vegetales y filigranas. Las iniciales de principio de canto miden entre 85 y 98 milímetros de alto y entre 60 y 67 milímetros de ancho, con los mismo colores rojo, azul y papel de oro. Para versos de introito , gradual y alleluia, las iniciales son negras con filigrana gruesa. El pergamino es de calidad media, y presenta signos de uso y roturas en el margen inferior exterior.  Foliación en el margen superior derecho en cifras arábicas.     En el interior de la cubierta, sobre papel añadido de forma posterior, alberga un índice del contenido ordenado por género.      En el último folio hay la rúbrica In festo Semidu. indicando que originalmente continuaba     Medidas provisionales*

title: (Palma) C18
description: a     El libro que contiene las misas propias del temporal, desde adviento hasta la segunda semana de cuaresma, es un cantoral de grandes dimensiones, con cubiertas de madera semiforradas en cuero (729 × 466 mm), reforzadas con remaches no decorativos y cierres en buen estado. Consta de 149 folios de pergamino (665× 460mm) y un último folio adherido al interior de la contraportada que proviene de un kyriale. El documento es de una única mano con disposición de 6 líneas de pentagrama (68mm de alto) por folio. La caja de escritura de 560× 320 mm. Las capitulares, tanto las iniciales de festividad como las de canto son simples de color rojo de entre 90 y 100mm de alto y 40 de largo. Las iniciales de los versículos son de doble línea gruesa en negra con las que se crean diseños geométricos y de tamaños similares al resto de iniciales. La única excepción es la primera capitular del cantoral que usa verde, rojo y amarillo con decoraciones de nudos de inspiración floral y encuadrada con varios marcos     El estado de conservación es en general bueno, aunque parte de los pergaminos están arrugados por culpa de la humedad que se agrava en los folios exteriores de ambas caras.  La calidad del pergamino es regular. Foliación, presumiblemente posterior al documento, en cifras arábicas.

description: Missale romanum d'Italie du Nord adapté à l'abbaye d'Andechs Missel qui paraît d'origine italienne, à en juger par l'écriture du texte, les abréviations et la série des versets alléluiatiques. Le texte littéraire a été écrit au IXe siècle; la notation, qui n'avait pas été prévue à l'origine, a été ajoutée au XIe-XIIe siècle par plusieurs mains allemandes, dont le travail est peu soigné. Le Missel est passé par Wessobrunn, avant d'être mis à l'usage de Saint-Nicolas d'Andechs. Notation neumatique allemande. (Extrait de GR II)

title: Porrentruy, Bibliothèque cantonale jurassienne, 18 (Bellelay Gradual)
description: At Bellelay Abbey from as early as 1160 until the suppression of the Abbey in 1797, the Bellelay Gradual has unknown origins. Although an important Premonstratensian manuscript of the Jurassian region, it is likely that the manuscript originated from north-eastern France and was a gift to Bellelay Abbey at its founding. To that effect, the Messine notation is not typical of the Jurassian region, and the manuscript includes many erasures and corrections suggesting adaptation to local practice. Furthermore, only one saint in the Sanctorale is particular to the Jurassian region, St. Imer (Imier), and even this seems to be a later addition from the beginning of the 13th century. The manuscript may have been a gift from the mother house of Lac de Joux Abbey, itself a sister abbey to Saint-Martin de Laon in north-eastern France.

title: Benevento, Biblioteca Capitolare, V 19
description: The two sources together do not present the complete cycle of either Temporale or Sanctorale. There are two significant lacunae in MS 20 (noted in the catalogue above). Most of the material from the first through the fourteenth Sundays after Pentecost has been lost in the first lacuna and, in the second, nearly all of the unusual Beneventan Office for Transfiguration (6 August) as well as anything between that date and the feast of St. Laurence (10 August). Except for these lacunae, the content of each manuscript is liturgically continuous. However, a significant portion of the annual cycle is missing due to the apparent loss of folios from the beginning and/or end of both manuscripts. The Temporale is complete as one passes from the end of MS 20 (the last Sunday after Pentecost) to the beginning of MS 19 (the first Sunday of Advent). However, the end of Lent, including the Triduum, Easter itself, and the beginning of Eastertide have been lost between the end of MS 19 (Tuesday in the fourth week of Lent) and the beginning of MS 20 (Tuesday after Easter). In the Sanctorale there are gaps between Annunciation (25 March, the end of MS 19) and Mark the Evangelist (25 April, the beginning of MS 20); and between Cosmas and Damian (27 September, the end of MS 20) and Nicholas (6 December, the beginning of MS 19). There are no chants for the Commons, the Dedication of a Church, or the Office for the Dead. It is not clear why the two volumes were bound in different orderings (Sanctorale then Temporale in MS 19 and the reverse in MS 20). This arrangement explains in part the sections of the calendar that were lost at the end of both manuscripts: a modest portion of the Temporale at the end of MS 19 and the larger section of the Sanctorale at the end of MS 20. Kelly has identified several Offices in each of these manuscripts which contain antiphons that are Beneventan or have cadences or other features that are Beneventan in character. These are shown in the facsimiles that appear in Paléographie musicale 21.

title: I-Ma : D 84 inf.
description: Sacramentaire-Missel de Bobbio du IXème siècle (cf. Bischoff) en notation neumatique de type germanique avec quelques lettres significatives Missel de Bobbio; Xᵉ-XIᵉ siècle. Ce manuscrit comprend seulement le Temporal, depuis la Vigile de Noël jusqu'au dimanche octave de la Pentecôte. Notation neumatique de l'Italie du Nord, apparentée à celle de Saint-Gall. title: Cambrai, Bibliothèque municipale, 38 (olim 40)
description: Cambrai 38 is a rich source of chants and Offices not found in CAO ; several are printed in full within Analecta hymnica . They include Thomas Becket (Analecta hymnica vol. 13, pp. 242-5), Lambertus (Analecta hymnica vol. 26, 230-3), both Offices for Elizabeth of Hungary (Analecta hymnica vol. 25, pp. 253-8 and 260-4, respectively; the Finding of Firminus (Analecta hymnica vol. 13, pp. 145-7), and the Crown of Thorns (Analecta hynnica vol. 24, pp. 30-4). Because Cambrai 38 and Cambrai XVI both come from Cambrai cathedral, there is considerable overlap between these two sources. Offices that are contained fully or partially in both manuscripts include Corpus Christi, Vedastus, Mary Magdalene, Gaugericus, Augustine, the Elevation of Elizabeth of Hungary, and Catherine. Because of Cambrai's proximity to Arras (at one time they were under the same bishop), Cambrai 38 and Arras 893 also have features in common; however, Arras 893 follows the monastic cursus, so its Offices do not correspond exactly to those in Cambrai 38. The Offices of Corpus Christi, Nicasius, the Finding of Firminus, and Vedastus appear in both of these manuscripts.Each chant not found in CAO is assigned an arbitrary number prefixed by cam. Differentiae are identified with numbers chosen arbitrarily; the numbering of differentiae in this file corresponds to that in the file for Cambrai XVI.

title: Cambrai, Bibliothèque municipale, Impr. XVI C 4
description: Cambrai XVI C 4, like Cambrai 38, is a rich source of chants and Offices not found in CAO . Offices found only in the former source include Barbara, Furse, Antoninus, Martialis, Anne, Donatus and Amatus (for Offices common to both files, please consult the introductory file to Cambrai 38). Cambrai XVI C 4 also contains lesson tones not found in Cambrai 38: the Vox dicentes and Liber generationis Jesu lessons and tones for the Lamentations of Jeremiah. Of particular note is the special Office, the Recollectio Mariae, dedicated in Cambrai cathedral by the canon Michel de Beringhen in 1457. The texts are by Giles Carlier, dean of Cambrai, and the chants were composed by Guillaume Dufay. (For more on this unique Office, see Haggh , The Celebration of the Recollectio Festorum Beatae Mariae Virginis 1457-1987.)Differentiae are identified by numbers chosen arbitrarily; the numbering system for this file is also used in the file for Cambrai 38. However, there are gaps in the numbering of the differentiae in this file, because not all of the differentiae of Cambrai reappear in this source.Each chant not found in CAO is assigned an arbitrary number, prefixed either by cam or cax: those chants beginning with cam can also be found in Cambrai 38, whereas the chants beginning with cax appear only in Cambrai XVI.

title: E-Bbc (Barcelona) Ms. 3180
description: Shelf-mark: Ms. 3180.     Date: fifteenth century.     Provenance: Cartuja de Valldemossa (Mallorca).     Physical description: 179 ff.: parchment with additions in paper (ff. 1-2 y 179); 320 x 220 mm. Old foliation with Roman numerals in black ink in the upper right-hand margin of the recto. Modern foliation with Arabic numerals in black ink in the upper right-hand margin of the recto. It is the work of a single main scribe. The additions in f. 178v are from the same period, and of a later period in f. 179. Binding with leather-covered boards.     Layout of the script: eight lines of text and music written in a single column.     Decoration: capitals decorated in red and blue, alternating with initials highlighted in yellow.     Musical notation: square notation on a red staff. F and C clefs and a custos.     Content summary: chants of the Mass (ff. 1-138v). Proper of Saints (ff. 139r-169r). Mass for the Dead (ff. 169v-171r). Chants of the Ordinary (ff. 172v-178r). Chants dedicated to Saint Anne on f. 178v. Chants for the feast of the Guardian Angel and the Common of the Mother of God on f. 179, written in a later hand.                 Signatura: Ms. 3180.     Datación: siglo XV.     Procedencia: Cartuja de Valldemossa (Mallorca).     Descripción física: 179 ff.: pergamino y añadidos en papel (ff. 1-2 y 179); 320 x 220 mm. Foliación antigua con numeración romana a tinta negra en el margen superior derecho del recto. Foliación moderna con numeración arábiga a tinta negra en el margen superior derecho del recto. Obra de un copista principal. Añadidos de la misma época (f. 178v) y posterior (f. 179). Encuadernación en piel sobre tabla.     Disposición de la escritura: 8 líneas de texto y música a línea tirada.     Decoración: Capitales adornadas en rojo y azul, alternas con iniciales realzadas en amarillo.     Notación musical: Notación cuadrada sobre tetragrama rojo. Claves de fa y do y guion final.     Resumen del contenido: Cantos de la Misa (ff. 1-138v). Propio de los Santos (ff. 139r-169r). Misa de difuntos (ff. 169v-171r). Cantos del Ordinario (ff. 172v-178r). Cantos dedicados a Santa Ana en el f. 178v. Cantos de la festividad del Ángel Custodio y del Común de la Madre de Dios en el f. 179, escritos con factura tardía.

title: E-Bbc (Barcelona) Ms. 3199
description: Signatura: Ms. 3199 Datación: siglo XV Procedencia: Cataluña Descripción física: 50 ff.: pergamino y añadidos en papel; 240 x 195 mm. Obra de diferentes manos. Encuadernación del siglo XVII en piel marrón sobre tabla con cierres metálicos. Disposición de la escritura: 5 líneas de texto y música a línea tirada. Decoración: Capitales adornadas y alternas en rojo y azul. Notación musical: Notación cuadrada sobre tetragrama rojo. Claves de fa y do y guión final. Resumen del contenido: Misa de difuntos (ff. 1-10). Cantos para el Oficio de difuntos, Domingo de Ramos, algunas Lamentaciones de Jeremías, Pasión según San Mateo y 8 entonaciones de la doxología menor (ff. 11-34). Invitatorio de maitines de Pascua (ff. 35-45). Antífonas para las festividades de San Juan de Capestrano, San Bernardino y Cadenas de San Pedro (ff. 46-50), lo que muestra su uso en Italia a pesar de su procedencia.

title: E-TAha (Tarragona) Ms. 22/1
description: Signatura: Ms. 22/1 Datación: siglo IX, ex. (Garrigosa); siglos IX-X, c. 900 (Janini) Procedencia: según Garrigosa, probablemente alguna parroquia de la zona fronteriza de la Catalunya Vella Descripción física: 1 bifolio: pergamino; 298 x 222 mm. Disposición de la escritura: 30 líneas distribuidas a 2 columnas. Escritura de notario rural de la época condal catalana (según Janini). Estado de conservación: no está en muy buen estado. Notación musical: Notación catalana arcaica sin pauta. A pesar de que se previó la colocación de los neumas en el manuscrito, el espacio resulta insuficiente en muchos lugares y los neumas aparecen hacinados. Resumen del contenido: Libro místico, mezcla de antifonario y leccionario de la Misa. Lecturas y cantos para la liturgia entre el Lunes Santo y el Jueves Santo.

title: E-Bbc (Barcelona) Ms. 2545
description: Shelf-mark: Ms. 2545.     Date: fourteenth-fifteenth centuries.     Provenance: Catalonia or the South of France (?)     Physical description: 240 ff.: parchment; 475 x 320 mm. Modern foliation with Arabic numerals in pencil in the upper right-hand margin of the recto. It is the work of a single main Scribe. Cloth binding on cardboard. There is a missing folio between f. 11 and f. 12.     Layout of the script: 9 lines of text and music in a single column. The first and last folios have a two-column arrangement.     Decoration: capitals in red and blue, often alternating between colours. Some capitals are greatly embellished.     Musical notation: square on a red staff. F and C clefs and a custos.     Content summary: antiphons, responsories and other chants for the major hours of the Proper of Time. Proper of Saints. Tonary (ff. 1r-4r). Hymnal (ff. 232r-240v).                 Signatura: Ms. 2545.     Datación: siglos XIV-XV.     Procedencia: Cataluña o sur de Francia (?)     Descripción física: 240 ff.: pergamino; 475 x 320 mm. Foliación moderna con numeración arábiga a lápiz en el margen superior derecho del recto. Obra de un copista principal. Encuadernación en tela sobre cartón. Falta un folio entre los ff. 11 y 12.     Disposición de la escritura: 9 líneas de texto y música a línea tirada. Los primeros y últimos folios están distribuidos a 2 columnas.     Decoración: Capitales en rojo y azul, a menudo alternas. Algunas capitales muy adornadas.     Notación musical: Notación cuadrada sobre tetragrama rojo. Claves de fa y do y guion final.     Resumen del contenido: Antífonas, responsorios y otros cantos para las horas mayores del Propio del Tiempo. Propio de los Santos. Tonario (ff. 1r-4r). Himnario (ff. 232r-240v).

title: E-Hbp (Huesca) Ms. 113
description: Shelf-mark: Ms. 113.     Date: fourteenth-fifteenth centuries.     Provenance: Cathedral of Lérida (indication in a liturgical rubric: “Incipiunt responsoria ad omnia altaria ecclesiae sedis illerdensis” [f. 56v]).     Physical description: 94 ff.: parchment; 195 x 140 mm. Text block 143 x 115 mm. Unbound. Late Arabic foliation in black ink in the upper right-hand corner; in all likelihood it was added after the loss of the original due to trimming. The manuscript is composed of twelve gatherings, mostly quaternions. Catchwords on ff. 8, 26, 36, 44, 52 and 60, except on the final folio of the second gathering, which is missing. The nineth and tenth gatherings do not have catchwords in order to put them together, nor do the last two.     Layout of the script: twelve lines of text and music written in a single column, alternating ruling (16 mm) and lines of text (8mm).     State of conservation: in all probability, the codex has undergone a trimming process. Nonetheless, the proportions of the outside margins are similar in every folio. Due to bookworms and the absence of binding, only the first and last folios are in poor condition.     Script: Gothic book script in black ink.     Musical notation: square notation on a red staff. F and C clefs and a custos.     Content summary: Officium parvum Beata Mariae Virginis; antiphonae et responsoria processionales; cantica varia.                 Signatura: Ms. 113.     Datación: siglos XIV-XV.     Procedencia: Catedral de Lérida (indicación en rúbrica litúrgica: “Incipiunt responsoria ad omnia altaria ecclesiae sedis illerdensis” [f. 56v]).     Descripción física: 94 ff.: pergamino; 195 x 140 mm. Caja de 143 x 115 mm. Sin encuadernación. Foliación tardía arábiga en el ángulo superior derecho en tinta negra; con toda probabilidad se realizó tras perderse la original en un guillotinado. El manuscrito consta de 12 fascículos, predominando los cuaterniones. Reclamos en ff. 8, 26, 36, 44, 52 y 60, sin embargo, falta el del desaparecido último folio del segundo fascículo. Los fascículos 9º y 10º no tienen reclamo para su unión, tampoco los dos últimos.     Disposición de la escritura: 12 líneas de texto y música a línea tirada, alternándose pautado (16 mm) y líneas textuales (8 mm).     Estado de conservación: El códice ha sufrido, con toda probabilidad, un proceso de guillotinado pero a pesar de ello las proporciones de los márgenes exteriores son similares en todos sus folios. Debido a la ausencia de encuadernación y por ataque de bibliófagos únicamente se encuentran en mal estado el primero y el último folio.     Escritura textual: Gótica libraria en tinta negra.     Notación musical: Notación cuadrada sobre pentagrama rojo. Claves de Fa y Do. Guion final.     Resumen del contenido: Officium parvum Beata Mariae Virginis; antiphonae et responsoria processionales; cantica varia.

title: E-VI (Vic) Ms. 105 (olim Còdex, CXI)
description: Signatura: Ms. 105 (olim Còdex, CXI) Datación: ss. XI-XII (Fdez. de la Cuesta/Gudiol); s. XII (Garrigosa); s. XII, in. (Gros) Procedencia: Gros afirma que no hay cantos para la fiesta de Sant Benito, y por tanto, debió ser copiado en la misma Catedral de Vic para el propio uso. Gros sugiere que el copista sería probablemente Berenguer Pere, que también habría copiado la música. Descripción física: 85 ff.: pergamino; 213 x 142 mm (Fdez. de la Cuesta/Gudiol); 215 x 140 mm (Garrigosa/Gros). Caja de escritura: 165 x 110 mm. Códice incompleto al principio y al final. Foliación moderna en numeración arábiga. Encuadernación en piel negra antigua sobre cartón de principios del siglo XIX. Todo el manuscrito presenta muchos añadidos y, por tanto, muchas manos. En el lomo se lee la siguiente inscripción: Liber antiphonarius cum notis musicis antiquis. Disposición de la escritura: Generalmente 11 líneas de texto a línea tirada. Decoración: Rúbricas de color rojo e iniciales en negro, rojo y los dos simultáneamente. Notación musical: Hay diversos tipos de notación, fruto del uso continuado del códice: - Notación catalana sin pauta, original del manuscrito (ff. 1-45; 63v-70v; 71v-77v). - Notación catalana ligeramente posterior (f. 46). - Notación aquitana sobre pauta roja y amarilla del s. XII, 2ª mitad (ff. 47r-58r). - Notación aquitana sobre pauta roja, clave de Fa y guión final, del s. XII, 2ª mitad (ff. 58v-60v). - Notación aquitana sobre cuatro pautas, una roja, una amarilla y dos a punta seca, con claves de Fa y Do y guión final, de finales del s. XII (ff. 62r-63r; 70v-71r; 78r-85v). Resumen del contenido: Contiene una gran cantidad de cantos rítmicos, prosas y tropos en el tropario-prosario, continuando con un Kyriale (ff. 47-60) y finalizando con folios añadidos en el siglo XIII (ff. 78-85).

title: E-VI (Vic) Ms. 66 (olim Còdex, XLVIII)
description: Signatura: Ms. 66 (olim Còdex, XLVIII)     Datación: año 1038, según inscripción del f. 100v en la que se deja constancia de que la copia se realizó para la nueva consagración de la catedral (2 de septiembre de 1038): Anni domini ab incarnatione MXXXVIII. Sic fuit ecclesiam sancti Petri in Vico dedicata II kalendas Septimbris, anno VIII regni Henrici, et iste libellus scriptus in praefata sede, in praedicto tempore, in diebus domini Olive anno ordinationis sue in episcopatu XXI.     Procedencia: Catedral de Vic, confeccionado por el canónigo Ermemir Quintiliano (según Garrigosa). Monasterio de Ripoll (según Fdez. de la Cuesta).     Descripción física: 131 ff.: pergamino; 335 x 260 mm. Caja de escritura: 260 x 190 mm. Mútilo al principio. Foliación moderna en numeraciones romana y arábiga. Encuadernación en piel negra antigua sobre cartón. En el lomo se lee la siguiente inscripción: XLVIII. Missale juxta odinem Romanae [Ecc]lesiae.     Disposición de la escritura: 26 líneas de texto distribuido a 2 columnas.     Estado de conservación: El manuscrito conserva hermosos márgenes, a pesar de haber sido recortados por parte del encuadernador, desapareciendo parte de las notas marginales. Pergamino grueso y fuerte, bastante blanco, la mayor parte algo amarillento y hasta rojizo. Muy deteriorado en los ff. I-XVI por efecto de la humedad.     Notación musical: Notación catalana sin pauta.     Resumen del contenido: Conocido como el Sacramentario de Vic, llamado también Sacramentario del obispo Oliva. Es de destacar la inclusión del rito mozárabe de la santa unción pero con música gregoriana en las antífonas (f. 80v). Cuenta con notación musical en algunos folios: ff. 23v, 82, 90r y 101r. Contenido primitivo del libro litúrgico: Misas del Temporal; Misas del Propio de los santos; Misas del Común de los santos; Misas votivas; oracional; dos Misas pro his qui a daemonio uexantur; dos oraciones contra daemonium; la Benedictio arrharum y el Ordo thalami, con la Missa pro Sponsis; ritual pro iter agentibus; Exorcismus salis et aquae y la bendición del agua; bendiciones de la casa y otras; Ordo unctionis seu pontificalis sive presbyteralis, con lo demás del Ordo infirmorum y sus correspondientes misas; Ordo defunctorum y Missae defuncorum.Prefacios y antífonas correspondientes al ritual de la Extrema Unción. A partir del f. 100 hay una serie de añadiduras, en general, de mano primitiva: Missa sanctorum omnium communis; Praefatio propria sancti Petri; VII idus januarii: Sancti Iuliani et Basilissae; II nonas octobris: Sanctae Fides virginis et martyris; Missa in dedicatione ecclesiae; Benedictio tumuli; Missa pro seipso sacerdote; VIII kalendas novembris: Sanctorum innumerabilium martyrum; lista de misas de difuntos; Penitencial.

title: E-Bbc (Barcelona) Ms. 619
description: Signature: Ms. 619 Dating: 13th century (Anglés / Garrigosa / Zauner); 12th-13th centuries (Janini); 13th-14th centuries (Fdez. de la Cuesta); 1175-1250 (Online Catalog of the Library of Catalonia) Provenance: Cathedral of Vic (Barcelona) Physical description: 135 ff.: parchment; 368 x 261 mm (Anglés / Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini); 370 x 260 mm (Garrigosa); 360 x 265 mm (Zauner); 360 x 270 mm (Online Catalog of the Library of Catalonia). Ancient foliation with Roman numerals in black ink on the upper right margin of the recto. Modern foliation with Arabic numerals in pencil on the upper right margin of the recto. Work of a main scribe with later additions on ff. 1r and 135r-v. It includes the colophon: Finito libro reddatur gratia Christo. Petrus sacerdos de Boxeda qui me scripsit (With the book finished, may grace be given to Christ. Peter, priest of Boxeda, who wrote me). Brown leather binding on cardboard. Layout of the script: 13 lines of text and music on ruled lines. Condition: Very good preservation. Decoration: Decorated capitals in red, green, occasionally yellow. Musical notation: Aquitaine notation on a tetragram with two dry-point staff lines, one red and one yellow. Square notation on a tetragram in black or red. Square notation on a tetragram with red and yellow staff lines (ff. 1r, 5, 7, 17, 27v, 33v, 52v, 55v, 56r, 57v, 58r, 65v, 66v, 76v, 77v, 78r, 91r, 107v, 109r, 114v, and 135). Fa and C clefs and final barline. Summary of content: Temporal cycle from the First Sunday of Advent to the Octave of Pentecost (ff. 1v-58v). Summer ferial antiphons for the Gospel canticle of Vespers (ff. 66v-71v). Proper of the Saints, from Saint Nicholas to Saint Andrew (ff. 73-127). Common of the Saints (ff. 127-133). 15th-century addition with eight intonations of the Gloria Patri, eleven Benedicamus Domino, and two Ite missa est (f. 1r). Signatura: Ms. 619 Datación: siglo XIII (Anglés / Garrigosa / Zauner); siglos XII-XIII (Janini); siglos XIII-XIV (Fdez. de la Cuesta); 1175-1250 (Catálogo on-line de la Biblioteca de Catalunya) Procedencia: Catedral de Vic (Barcelona) Descripción física: 135 ff.: pergamino; 368 x 261 mm (Anglés / Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini); 370 x 260 mm (Garrigosa); 360 x 265 mm (Zauner); 360 x 270 mm (Catálogo on-line de la Biblioteca de Catalunya). Foliación antigua con numeración romana a tinta negra en el margen superior derecho del recto. Foliación moderna con numeración arábiga a lápiz en el margen superior derecho del recto. Obra de un copista principal con añadidos posteriores en los ff. 1r y 135r-v. Aparece el colofón: Finito libro reddatur gratia Christo. Petrus sacerdos de Boxeda qui me scripsit. Encuadernación en piel marrón sobre cartón. Disposición de la escritura: 13 líneas de texto y música a línea tirada. Estado de conservación: Muy buena conservación. Decoración: Capitales adornadas en rojo, verde, ocasionalmente en amarillo. Notación musical: Notación aquitana sobre tetragrama con dos pautas a punta seca, una roja y otra amarilla. Notación cuadrada sobre tetragrama negro o rojo. Notación cuadrada sobre tetragrama con pautas rojas y amarillas (ff. 1r, 5, 7, 17, 27v, 33v, 52v, 55v, 56r, 57v, 58r, 65v, 66v, 76v, 77v, 78r, 91r, 107v, 109r, 114v y 135) Claves de fa y do y guión final. Resumen del contenido: Ciclo temporal desde el Domingo I de Adviento hasta la Octava de Pentecostés (ff. 1v-58v). Antífonas feriales estivales para el cántico evangélico del Oficio de vísperas (ff. 66v-71v). Propio de los Santos, desde San Nicolás hasta San Andrés (ff. 73-127). Común de los Santos (ff. 127-133). Añadido del siglo XV con ocho entonaciones del Gloria Patri, once Benedicamus Domino y dos Ite missa est (f. 1r).

description: This fragment covered a book with documents from the monastery of Sanfins de Friestas (Valença), near the northern Portuguese border. The monastery and its properties were given to the Jesuits by the King in 1545, who took possession (after some reconstruction work) in 1554; this was intended as a means to support expenses related to the Colégio de Jesus, founded in Coimbra in 1542. With the extinction of the Order, the College's administrative documents (including those concerning Sanfins de Friestas) entered the University archives. From the same book another fragment survives, P-Cua IV-3ª Gav. 44 (03). Both fragments show close proximity with the antiphoner E-Tc 44.2; a few chants are found, however, among early notated sources, only in E-Tc 44.1; the breviaries of Braga and Évora are also closely related.

title: P-Cua (Coimbra) Arquivo Distrital e da Universidade IV-3ª Gav. 44 (03)
description: From the same book as P-Cua IV-3ª Gav. 44 (20), which was used as a cover for administrative registers at the College of Jesus. The musical and liturgical contents of this fragment show a close proximity with the same feasts as found in Toledo, Catedral - Archivo y Biblioteca Capítulares, 44.2. The same can be seen in the related fragment Gav. 44 (20).  NOTES ON THE CHANT INDEX: The Responsory 'Simile est regnum' (CI 602213) is only found in Iberian sources and in the Antiphoner from Marseille cathedral F-Pnm lat. 1090, dated between 1190 and 1200. See http://cantusindex.org/id/602213. The Responsory 'Domine si tu es' (CI 006515) is paired with the Verse 'Cumque vidisset' (CI 006515zb), which contains a textual variant so far only found among Iberian manuscripts. See http://cantusindex.org/id/006515. The Responsory 'Ego pro te' (CI 006630) is paired with the Verse 'Simon ecce Satanas' (CI 006630zd), normally found in Iberian manuscripts. See http://cantusindex.org/id/006630zd.

title: P-Cm (Coimbra) Biblioteca Municipal FPM-B50-09
description: The recto includes a rubric apparently requiring the use of the common of confessors for Fernando, a priest (ffernadi confessoris); the position of the commemoration implies a date between 13 and 15 of June; the only saint of that name and category is Fernando (or Fernam) Martins de Bulhões, the secular name of St. Anthony, who spent some time in Santa Cruz de Coimbra before becoming a Franciscan and is commemorated on June 13th, which fits the calendar. The verso has part of the mass for the Vigil of John the Baptist, and apparently two masses for the feast day. The rubric before the decorated 'A' instructs that the first mass is de luce, at sunrise. The second mass is that in die, although its rubric (right end of the seventh line) is undecipherable. While the main mass does not pose any particular problem and the choice of chants is wholly regular, an aurora mass for John the Baptist is unusual. It might thus be that the fragment comes from an institution with strong ties to this saint; since the external features of the document are compatible with a local origin, this was perhaps São João das Donas, a feminine convent dependent on Santa Cruz de Coimbra, whose patron was St. John the Baptist.  This accords with the the unusual rubric referred to above, since Dona Constança Sanches (1204-1269), natural daughter of King Sancho I, professed in this convent in 1224 and had an altar and a chapel erected to St. Anthony shortly after his canonization in 1232. She is said to have met him in Coimbra before her profession when he was at Santa Cruz and responded to the name Fernando, leaving a lasting impression on the young Constança; she left provisions to be buried in his chapel (Santa Maria, Chronica, pp. 541-543). This fragment, in its mention of Fernando instead of Antonio, probably replicates an earlier manuscript that preserved the 13th-century local memory of the saint.

title: E-Gs (Girona) ms. 45
provenance: Colegiata de Sant Feliu de Girona
description: There is a possibility that this manuscript belongs to the cultural milieu of canon Renall in Barcelona, as it mentions the feast of Saint Eulalia and not that of Saint Felix. Subsequently, Renall took it to Girona. It is currently located in the Museu d’Art de Girona.     Physical description: Manuscript of 164 folios of 245 x 195 mm. Leather binding from the nineteenth century with the title “Cantus Breviarii antiquissimus moderator” on the spine. The script consists of 17 to 19 lines of text and music written in a single column in a text block of 195 x 135 mm. Some changes of hand are observed in the script of the text and musical notation, although, on some occasions, it may just be attributed to changes of quill. There are several antiphons that have been added afterwards on different folios. It is in fairly good condition, despite the binding appearing to be disorderly. Initials written with quill in yellow and ochre.     Notation: Diastematic Catalan. From folio 109 onwards there is a much more diastematic notation based on points (punctum). On folio 39, there is a verbeta (responsorial prosula) in notation that dates back to the eleventh century. On folio 140, a four-line staff has been added alongside the notation.     Content: From the Saturday before Passion Sunday to Saint John the Baptist. It contains several verbetas (responsorial prosulas).                  Es probable que este manuscrito pertenezca al entorno cultural del canónigo Renall en Barcelona, ya que menciona la fiesta de Santa Eulalia y no la de San Félix. Posteriormente, Renall lo llevó a Girona. Actualmente se encuentra en el Museu d'Art de Girona.     Descripción física: manuscrito de 164 folios, 245x195 mm. Encuadernación en piel, del siglo XIX, con el título en el lomo Cantus Breviarii antiquissimus moderator. Escritura tirada de 17 a 19 líneas de texto con música en caja de 195x135mm. Se observan algunos cambios de mano en la escritura del texto y en la notación musical, aunque a veces puede tratarse solo de cambios de pluma. Hay algunas antífonas añadidas posteriormente en diferentes folios. Está en bastante buen estado, aunque parece desordenado en la encuadernación. Iniciales a pluma en amarillo y ocre.     Notación: catalana diastemática. A partir del folio 109 encontramos una notación mucho más diastémica, basada en puntos. En el folio 39 hay una verbeta en notación que data del siglo XI. En el folio 140 se ha añadido un tetragrama junto a la notación.     Contenido: desde el sábado anterior al domingo de Pasión hasta de San Juan Bautista. Contiene varias verbetas.

description: Descripción física: 104 folios, 485 × 350 mm, pergamino. Encuadernación original con cubiertas de madera unidas mediante un lomo de cuero y tachuelas, con restos de un cierre metálico. En el interior de ambas cubiertas se conservan fragmentos de pergamino con música en notación cuadrada en tinta negra sobre pentagrama rojo, que funcionan como hojas de guarda. Estado del códice: Códice mútilo debido a la pérdida de varios folios al comienzo, en el cuerpo del volumen y al final. Presenta foliación a lápiz en los márgenes superiores derechos y un número en rojo acompañado de un asterisco (2*) al inicio del documento, que parece corresponder a una antigua signatura. Se observan marcas de uso y señales de reparación a lo largo de todo el manuscrito. Decoración: Iniciales de los responsorios en colores azul y rojo alternados, con adornos caligráficos; texto y notación musical en tinta negra; epígrafes y rúbricas en tinta roja. Notación musical: Notación cuadrada sobre dos líneas de referencia: la línea inferior en tinta amarilla (color desvaído) para el do, y la línea superior en tinta roja para el fa. Resumen del contenido: Contiene responsorios con sus respectivos versículos y verbetas de todo el año litúrgico, comenzando por el segundo domingo de Adviento (códice acéfalo) y finalizando con la festividad De prophetis (de las historias de verano), también incompleto. Estado de conservación: Las cubiertas (y las hojas de guarda) están parcialmente carcomidas y desgastadas. El cuerpo del manuscrito presenta un alto grado de deterioro debido a mutilaciones, tinta corroída, fragmentos borrados, carcoma, marcas de productos químicos (cola) y palimpsestos.

title: E-Mh (Madrid) Cód. 112
description: Signatura: Cód. 112 (Signatura antigua: 11-2-6/402) Datación: Siglo XIV Procedencia: Convento franciscano de Villacastín (Segovia) Descripción física: Manuscrito facticio. 109 folios: pergamino; 220 x 165 mm (Ruiz); 220 x 170 mm (web BRAH). Los ff. 101r-104v proceden de otro ms., probablemente extrapeninsular. Encuadernación antigua, en tabla forrada de una piel de color corinto. Disposición de la escritura: Texto y música a línea tirada (16 líneas en los ff. 1-100), unidad de pautado: 9-10 mm. Estado de conservación: En buen estado. Escritura textual: Escritura gótica fracturada, de pequeño módulo y esmerado trazado, de tipo litúrgico. Decoración: Las iniciales primarias son mayúsculas góticas con filigranas. En el campo interior aparece de vez en cuando dibujado un rostro. Las iniciales secundarias son desnudas. Los colores empleados son rojo y morado. Entre los ff. 101r-104v figuran unas iniciales de mejor factura y realizadas con pigmentos de variados y delicados tonos (azul grisáceo, rojo intenso y verde). Notación musical: Notación cuadrada sobre pauta roja y guión final en los ff. 105r-109v. Resumen del contenido: Calendario (ff. 7r-12v), Missa Sancte Marie (f. 15r), Missa pro fidelibus defunctis (f. 100v), Missa contra persecutores et male agentes (101r-104v) y textos litúrgicos en honor a San Blas con notación musical.

title: Dubrovnik, Franjevački samostan Male braće - Zbirka franjevačkog samostana na Badiji (Franciscan Monastery of the Friars Minor - The Badija Collection), Badija X
description: The four-volume Dominican antiphoner (Badija III, V, X, and XI) forms part of the Badija collection of medieval choir books housed in the Franciscan Monastery of the Friars Minor in Dubrovnik. Together with the corresponding volumes of the gradual–kyriale–sequentiary (MSS Badija IV and Badija XII), these choir books constitute a complete liturgical set for Mass and Office. The volumes came into the possession of the Dubrovnik friars in 1949, after the Second World War, when the Franciscan monastery on the island of Badija, near Korčula, was expropriated and the medieval choir books from its library were transferred to the Monastery of the Friars Minor in Dubrovnik. Based on the analysis of the Litany of the Saints in the gradual Badija XII, it has been possible to establish Zadar as the provenance of the entire liturgical set. This provenance, however, refers only to the place where the manuscripts were in use until 1807, namely the Dominican convent of St Dominic in Zadar. A detailed examination of the liturgical content, which corresponds to the codex exemplar of the Dominican liturgy (Rome, Santa Sabina, XIV L1), suggests that the Badija choir books were produced between 1256 and 1300. On the basis of their illumination, Andrea Improta has proposed a date between 1260 and 1280, probably in the Italian region of Emilia-Romagna, owing to similarities with choir books illuminated by the Master of Bagnacavallo (in particular the antiphoner Bagnacavallo, Biblioteca Comunale Taroni, MSS 1–3). This dating has been further corroborated by a palaeographical analysis of the square chant notation, which has shown the Badija choir books to be highly concordant with the five-volume antiphoner copied for the Dominicans of Imola around 1275 (Imola, Museo Diocesano, Corali 5, 6, 7, 9, 10).

A detailed examination of the liturgical content, which corresponds to the codex exemplar of the Dominican liturgy (Rome, Santa Sabina, XIV L1), suggests that the Badija choir books were produced between 1256 and 1300. On the basis of their illumination, Andrea Improta has proposed a date between 1260 and 1280, probably in the Italian region of Emilia-Romagna, owing to similarities with choir books illuminated by the Master of Bagnacavallo (in particular the antiphoner Bagnacavallo, Biblioteca Comunale Taroni, MSS 1–3). This dating has been further corroborated by a palaeographical analysis of the square chant notation, which has shown the Badija choir books to be highly concordant with the five-volume antiphoner copied for the Dominicans of Imola around 1275 (Imola, Museo Diocesano, Corali 5, 6, 7, 9, 10).

title: Trier, Bistumsarchiv, Abt. 95, Nr. 5
description: The manuscript D-Trb Abt. 95, Nr. 5 (hereafter Trier 5) is a small book measuring 16.4 cm by 11.4 cm. Its 145 folios comprise three parts written in different hands. The first part is a legendary that contains saints' vitae (folios 1-103v). The second part consists of three proper offices for the Anglo-Saxon missionary siblings and Eichstätt patrons Willibald, Wunnebald, and Walburga (folios 104v-141). The change in hand and format between these sections, together with the fact that folios 104 and 141v were originally left empty, suggests that the offices were copied as nineteen bifolios, folded to create a libellus with a blank cover—a small book which could easily have been held in the cantor’s hand. Once bound with the legendary and additional pages, folios 141v- 145v were inscribed with additional hagiographic material. Written on the inside of the back cover is the sequence Magnificandus et omnicolendus for Pope Pascal II, who died in 1118. Due to this composite nature of the manuscript, estimates of its date have varied from late tenth-century to early twelfth-century. The eleventh-century chronicler Anonymous of Herrieden (Anonymus Haserensis) attributes the offices for Willibald and Wunnebald to Reginold, Bishop of Eichstätt from 966-991, and the Walburga office to the poet-composer Wolfhard von Herrieden, author of the late ninth-century Miracula S. Walburgae. The three offices follow the secular cursus and reflect the liturgy of the Eichstätt cathedral. The texts of the Walburga office are drawn from Wolfhard’s Miracula, while those for Willibald and Wunnebald follow the vitae composed by the nun Huneberc of Heidenheim. Dörr, Schlager, and Wohnhaas suggest that Reginold composed the office for Saint Willibald for the occasion of his translation on April 22nd, 989, providing a terminus post quem for the creation of the libellus that was later incorporated into Trier 5. I have suggested that Reginold’s offices for Willibald and Wunnebald were intended as the concluding members of a trilogy: one that elevated the two brothers, whose fame was previously eclipsed by that of their celebrated sister, and claimed the legacy of this trio of saints for the diocese. The conclusion of this proper office trilogy moreover established Reginold in a poetic and compositional lineage descending from Wolfhard of Herrieden.   The text of Trier 5 is written in Caroline miniscule. Many of the initials for the office texts were never completed. The manuscript’s adiastematic neumes use St. Gall forms, but without litterae significativae. The notational hand is characterized by long, tapered pen strokes with a prominent convex ductus. Reginold's remarkable trilingual trope Terminus et idem interminus for the last Matins responsory of the Willibald office was first described by Anonymous of Herrieden. The text linguistically retraces Willibald’s pilgrimage to Jerusalem by traveling through Latin, Greek, Hebrew and back through Greek to Latin. The trope is also transmitted independently from the office in D-Mü Clm 14377, from St. Emmeram in Regensburg. In both sources, the Greek and Hebrew portions of the text are transliterated into Latin characters. The transcription of the Hebrew portion of the trope found in the CANTUS Database is based on the transcription by Daniel et alia. The transcription of the Greek portions of the trope follows J. L. Van Dieten’s reconstruction. A complete translation of the trope into German may be found in Dörr, Schlager, and Wohnhaas. Wolfhard of Herrieden’s office for St. Walburga is also transmitted in the fragment D-Mü Clm 29316(5 (antiphoner, Salzburg, 10th-11th century.) Selected Matins responsories from the office are recorded in CZ-Pu VI.E.4c, a twelfth-century breviary from the convent of St. George in Prague, and in NL-ZUa 6, a fifteenth-century antiphoner from the chapter church of St. Walburga in Zutphen. The Lauds antiphons of the Walburga office are transmitted in the above sources, and in the fourteenth-century antiphoner CZ-Pu XIV.B.13 from the St. George convent. Finally, the magnificat antiphon for second vespers is transmitted in the Münster printed antiphonal of 1537. Textual evidence from printed breviaries shows that a modified version of the Walburga office was in use at the Eichstätt cathedral into the seventeenth century. Inside the back cover of the book (here indexed as folio 146) appears the addition of the un-notated sequence Magnificandus et omnicolendus for Pope Paschal II (1099-1118). My transcription adapts that of Thomas Haye for the first seventeen versicles.  This project was completed with a grant from the Graduate College of the University of Northern Iowa. My thanks go to Mother Franziska Kloos, Abbess of the Benedictine Abbey of St. Walburg, Eichstätt, and to the staffs of the Bistumsarchiv Trier, the special collections department of the Universitätsbibliothek Eichstätt-Ingolstadt, and the Hill Museum and Manuscript Library, St. John's University, for their research assistance.

title: Einsiedeln, Stiftsbibliothek, 611
description: Einsiedeln 611 records a few examples of an unusual practice of the monks of Einsiedeln, the singing of some chants at Nones, prior to a feast's First Vespers, in anticipation of the days of certain important saints. Such services (consisting of an antiphon or an antiphon with versicle in the manuscript) may be observed for the following feasts: John the Baptist (f. 184v), Peter (f. 189r), Assumption (f. 213v), and All Saints (f. 237r). The fact that such a Nones service is included for the Common of Apostles (f. 251r) may indicate that this practice was more general than only for those occasions given specific chants for this service in the manuscript. It is not clear whether these anticipatory Nones services were conflated with or replaced the Nones service of the preceding day.Some of the unusual Offices in Einsiedeln 611 have been edited in Analecta Hymnica and also appear in Andrew Hughes's Late Medieval Liturgical Offices, including Catherine (AH vol. 26, p. 69, LMLO CB24) and the so-called Historia nova for Benedict (AH vol. 25, p. 52, LMLO BE01) that appears in Einsiedeln 611 on the feast of his translation. The prose Office for Corpus Christi (often attributed to Thomas Aquinas) was not edited in AHbut was copied in LMLO under the siglum XCX. These Offices appear in several other sources in the Cantus database.Other saints' Offices have not been edited in AH nor do they appear in LMLO. These include Meinrad, the hermit-founder of Einsiedeln (21 January); Sigismundus, martyred King of Burgundy (1 May); Felix and Regula, martyrs (11 September); and significant portions of the Office for Maurice and his companions (22 September).There are only three invitatory tones that are written out in Einsiedeln 611. Presumably there were others on folios now lost. The three tones are those identified as GR, 5, and 3 in the Cantus database. For some of the tones represented only by incipit there is little doubt as to their identity: 2, 7, NE, HS, and PA. One tone (beginning DA, GF, GF) seems likely to be BL; another incipit (DA, AC, A) appears to refer both to the tone in general use on Christmas (CH) and to the tone represented as GR in the database.A final tone seems to be one of those that was written on a leaf now missing from Hartker's antiphoner (St. Gall 390-391); its presence there can be inferred from a copy of Hartker (St. Gall 388) that includes it at the corresponding point in the series. It has been given the siglum HL. St. Gall 388 (and presumably Hartker) assign two antiphons to it, Regem regum dominum and Surgite vigilemus. Einsiedeln 611 assigns the latter of these to the tone called 2 but assigns a second antiphon to this tone, Ploremus coram domino, for the feast of Mary Magdalene.The differentiae for each mode have been numbered with a two-digit system: a majuscule letter indicating the final pitch of the differentia and a sequentially-ordered numeral. For those differentiae that exist in slightly variant forms, minuscule letters (a-d) have been added as suffixes.

title: Einsiedeln, Stiftsbibliothek, Codex 121
description: This manuscript consists of two parts. The first part (pp.1-428) is the oldest complete surviving Gradual with adiastematic neumes. Besides the Mass chants, in order throughout the liturgical year, there are appendices of Alleluia verses, hymns, antiphons for several occasions, and a neumed versicularium (Psalmi ad Communionem). The first page(s) are missing; the Gradual starts with the Alleluia Ostende nobis Domine of the 1st Sunday in Advent. In the Gradual, the Temporale and Sanctorale are not separated. Verses for the offertories are given with neumes. The Gradual section is known for the extraordinary usage of litterae significativae within the neume notation.The second part of the codex (pp. 429-599) contains sequences by Notker from St. Gall (ca. 840-912); throughout this section the text forms the main body of each page with adiastematic neumes in the margins. The codex was written in Einsiedeln, likely for the third abbot of the cloister, Gregor the Englishman. Some chants are neumed by later hands. The pages of Einsiedeln 121 are numbered with a modern hand in black ink in the upper outside corners of the leaves (pp. 1-600); there is no original numbering. The manuscript includes various illuminated letters, mostly in the Gradual, and three large illustrations that cover the entire page: an ornamented monogram (p. 204: In die sancto Resurrectionis Domini ad Missam), the ornamented “Resurrexi” of Easter Sunday’s Introit (p. 205), and another ornamented monogram (p. 436: In nomine Domini incipit Lyber Ymnorum Notkeri).

title: Istanbul, Topkapı Sarayı Müzesi, Deissmann 42 (The Istanbul Antiphoner)
description: Provenance (origin): the ecclesiastical province of Esztergom of medieval Hungary during the Angevin period (Dobszay, 'The Origin and Fate of the Codex,” p. 62).Provenance (usage): Esztergom.Provenance (subsequent history): During the Turkish occupation of Hungary (1526-1686), the codex was taken as booty to Istanbul (Ibid.).Noteworthy details: In this codex are two complete Offices for Adalbert of Prague, the patron saint of the diocese of Esztergom: one for 23 April and one, commemorating the translation of Adalbert’s relics, for 6 November. According to Dobszay, the latter was a feast local to Esztergom (Dobszay, “The Liturgical Analysis of the Codex,” 47). The Sanctorale contains complete Offices for the following Hungarian saints: King Ladislaus, King Stephen I, Emeric and Elizabeth of Hungary. Added items at the end of the manuscript include two feasts prevalent in Hungarian sources: one for Queen Helen (mother of Emperor Constantine the Great) and one for Mary of the Snows (Ibid., 47, 52, 53).] The Istanbul Antiphoner is the only known source of the full Office for Andrew and Benedict that includes musical notation (Ibid., 51). Similarly, the Office for Anna contained in this source is known to appear in only one other source, the Esztergom Breviary (Ibid., 47).Contributors to MS Description: ES (2005), ed. DL (Dec. 2006) Two invitatory tones found in the Istanbul Antiphoner have not yet been identified in other sources. They have been assigned the codes IS (associated with mode 2 antiphons) and IT (associated with mode 5 antiphons). The latter is included only in incipit in the manuscript. In addition, the invitatory tone labelled as “KN” in reference to the Klosterneuburg manuscripts (Liber Hymnarius, 162) is included in the Istanbul antiphoner. The incipit of what appears to be the ferial invitatory tone FE (owing to its usage in the manuscript) does not correspond to any of the full tones listed at the end of the book. It is associated once with a mode 4 antiphon and otherwise with mode 6 antiphons.Marginalia that have not been indexed in this file owing to illegibility are referenced in the notes file (available from the CANTUS research office upon request).There are two sets of foliation in pencil; in cases where the two sets do not match, the upper one (sometimes in parentheses) has been followed.

title: Prague, Strahovská knihovna (Library of the Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DE I 7 (Breviarium Strigoniense)
description: Due to the secular cursus and the inclusion of liturgical aspects particular to Hungary (e.g., the responsorium prolixum Quam magnificata at second Vespers on Sundays per annum; the antiphon Ave spes  introducing second Vespers at Christmas; and the antiphona sola at Matins on the first three days of the Holy Week), the manuscript is of Hungarian diocesan provenance. More specifically, it is the earliest notated document of the Esztergom diocesan tradition. The writing technique in the manuscript also indicates that it was completed at the scriptorium of Esztergom. It is unknown when and how the breviary arrived at the Strahovská knihovna of the Klášter premonstrátů na Strahovĕ, the library of the famous Premonstratensian monastery of Prague, but Janka Szendrei suggests that it was likely acquired sometime in the eighteenth century.  The Sanctorale volume that would have accompanied this breviary is lost. The manuscript is written on parchment. The manuscript was rebound in the nineteenth century at which point some of the margins were cut and ff. 10 and 15 were exchanged and turned upside down. Modern foliation in pencil in upper right-hand corner of the recto side of each folios was completed after rebinding with several errors. Several leaves have been bound upside down: for example, 10 and 15 have been switched in binding so that the folio numbered as “10” in the manuscript = 15 with respect to content in the index (and “10v” in the manuscript = 15r with respect to content in the index). “15r” in the manuscript = 10v, and “15v” = 10r. The items on these folia have been inventoried according to their current locations in order that users will be able to locate them in the online images (available in manuscriptorium.com). The chant incipits have not been indexed from the long rubric on f. 3v. Differentiae are indexed by their last note and an arbitrarily-assigned number within each mode. The majority of text is written in one hand with the exception of ff. 206r-222v, which was completed by another scribe and one or more notators at approximately the same time as the rest of the manuscript. It is Gothic textualis formata for the majority of the manuscript and rotunda-like script for ff. 206r-222v.

The antiphon Quis dabit, whose text is here barely legible, is found together with the preceding antiphons in the printed Évora Breviary of 1528 but very few concordances (E-Tc 44.2, P-BRs Ms. 032) are known otherwise. It is possible that the fragment is an early witness to the liturgical use of Évora.

description: Graduel inséré dans un Sacramentaire. Pour chaque messe on trouve d'abord les pièces de chant groupées ensemble, puis les oraisons et les préfaces. Les Saints qui sont mentionnés dans ce manuscrit appartiennent à des provinces situées autour de l'Anjou. On peut donc penser à Angers comme lieu d'origine de notre manuscrit, d'autant plus que de très bonne heure il a fait partie du fonds de Saint-Aubin d'Angers. La mention de S. Pierre comme Patron de l'église semble indiquer que le manuscrit pourrait provenir de l'église Saint-Pierre d'Angers. Il est cependant difficile de dire avec certitude que ce Missel y a été écrit. En effet, les livres liturgiques d'Angers sont notés en neumes français, or Angers 91 est noté en neumes bretons. Rien n'indique jusqu'à présent que la notation bretonne ait été en usage à Angers. On peut donc supposer que ce manuscrit a été écrit dans un centre breton et apporté ensuite à Angers. Quelques additions en neumes français aux folios 220ᵛ et 223 ne contredisent pas cette supposition. Xᵉ siècle. Les mots du canon de la messe sont accentués. (Extrait de GR II)

title: F-PR : Ms 12
description: Graduel de Chartres, suivi du Kyriale (f. 239) et des séquences ; XIIIe siècle (entre 1205 et 1218). L'origine est déterminée par le Sanctoral. L'ordre des versets alléluiatiques est identique à celui des manuscrits de la Cathédrale de Chartres. Enfin les rubriques des Rogations mentionnent des églises de Chartres. Écriture et décoration du XIIIe siècle. L'absence de la fête de S. Guillaume et la séquence propre pour Ste Anne (f. 310) semblent indiquer que le manuscrit a été copié dans le premier tiers du XIIIe siècle, peut-être entre 1205 et 1218 (ou 1230). Les différences observées entre ce manuscrit et l'Ordinaire chartrain au XIIIe siècle (éd. Y. DELAPORTE, 1953) impliquent que le scribe a dû recopier un Graduel de la seconde moitié du XIIe siècle. Notation à points liés français sur 4 lignes tracées à la pointe sèche ; la ligne du fa est colorée en vert, celle du do était autrefois teintée de jaune. (Extrait de GR II)

title: F-Collection privée : Mont-Renaud
description: Graduel et Antiphonaire de Saint-Éloi de Noyon ; Xe siècle. Les messes sont capitulées. Le texte n'a pas été prévu pour être noté. La notation est cependant à peu près contemporaine de l'écriture du texte : neumes français de l'Ile-de-France. Le ton des antiennes d'introit et de communion est indiqué en marge. Extrait de GR II) Description matérielle : Parchemin, 133 feuillets, 230 × 145 mm. Notation neumatique française ajoutée postérieurement au texte (environ 50 ans après la transcription initiale), avec interventions secondaires en notation messine. Contenu  : Double livre liturgique comprenant : Graduel (ff. 1-48v) : chants de la messe, avec lacune importante des Rameaux à l'Ascension. Antiphonaire (ff. 49-107v) : chants de l'office, de type originellement monastique, adapté ultérieurement à l'usage séculier par des annotations marginales et interlinéaires. Origine  : Le texte aurait été copié à l'abbaye de Corbie mais pour l'usage de Noyon (monastère Saint-Éloi). La notation musicale en neumes corbéiens aurait été ajoutée plus tard à Noyon d'après un modèle de Corbie. Plusieurs éléments liturgiques le rattachent à l'abbaye de Saint-Denis. Particularités : Notation musicale ajoutée après la copie du texte, comme l'indique la disposition serrée de l'écriture sans séparation entre les syllabes. Sept mains différentes identifiables dans les notations musicales. Contient l'Office de la Sainte-Trinité composé par Étienne de Liège, ce qui situe sa rédaction après 920 Adaptation progressive d'un office monastique à l'usage canonial. Présence de saint Éloi et saint Étienne dans les litanies et le sanctoral, confirmant l'origine noyonnaise Historique : Connu du chanoine Morel, curé de Chevrières (Oise) avant 1914. Le château du Mont-Renaud fut attaqué pendant la Seconde Guerre mondiale, mais le manuscrit fut sauvé alors que la bibliothèque disparut. Découvert au Château du Mont-Renaud en 1874, son importance exceptionnelle fut reconnue en 1952 par le chanoine Jeanneteau.

La série des versets alléluiatiques est identique à celle de Saint-Pierre de Lille (Lille 26 = Lil) ; par ailleurs on trouve trois versets alléluiatiques pour S. Pierre. Enfin, les Saints des litanies (f. 85) se retrouvent presque tous au Bréviaire de Lille de 1533. Ce Graduel peut donc venir de Saint-Pierre de Lille. title: F-Togs : Ms 001
provenance: France, Tours, collégiale Saint-Martin de Tours
description: Missel de Saint-Martin de Tours ; début du XIᵉ siècle. Ce Missel n'a pas de Sanctoral. Notation neumatique française de Tours. Plusieurs pièces, en particulier après la Pentecôte, ne sont pas notées. (Extrait de GR II) --------------------------- Note de Dom Guy OURY : Ce missel a été étudié par L BOSSEBOEUF : Un Missel de Marmoutier du XIe s. dans Revue de l'Art Chrétien (Barbier de Montault)t.VII, 1889,p. 291-308 et 420-438 Le Missel a été écrit pour Marmoutier. Il a été ensuite utilisé pour l'église N.D. d'Avon dans le Chinonais (Indre et Loire). Le calendrier est enrichi d'un obituaire édité par L.Bosseboeuf art. cité p.305 . et l'on trouve plusieurs notes d'anniversaires f° 15 et 209v. (édit. Bosseboeuf) Le f°209 donne une charte complète concernant un litige entre le curé d'Avon et ses paroissiens (édit. Bosseboeuf). Dom Beyssac a collationné les parties éditées par L. Bosseboeuf sur l'original et a consigné dans une note manuscrite placée en tête de l'article en question, toutes les fautes de lecture. Le f°208 recopié au milieu du XIIe s. donne un poème français en 12 laisses monorimes, découvert par Dom Martène, paraphrasant librement Act.VI,8-9 et VII,55-59 et présenté comme la leçon de St. Estève à lire devant les laïcs assis (sans doute au cours même de la messe de St Etienne). Edit. G.Paris,1862, médiocre - Foerster-Koschwitz , Alt französisches Uebungsbuch Leipzig ,1932,s.167-171, 319-320. Edit. critique préparée par Mlle Callebaut. Cette pièce est connue des modernes sous le nom d'Epître farcie de St Etienne.

title: Budapest, Egyetemi Könyvtár (University Library), lat. 121

The history of these manuscripts is little known before they were acquired by the University Library of Budapest during the reign of Joseph II of Hungary (1780-90). That they were used by the Franciscan Order, however, is clear from a number of inscriptions in the manuscripts, and the occurrence of saints especially venerated by that order (i.e., Peter of Alcantara, Anthony of Padua, Clare, and Francis of Assisi). title: Quito, Iglesia de San Francisco - Archivo, 18P16
description: Since Didacus of Alcalá was canonized in 1588 by Pope Sixtus V and this manuscript includes a feast in his name, this manuscript was probably copied at the end of the 16th century after the arrival of the Franciscan commission to Quito in 1534 led by Jodocus Rickye and Pierre Gosseal who founded the Church and Convent. A colophon at 148r (fragmented) suggests that part of the manuscript may have been completed in 1600, as the fragmented date ends with a partially visible D followed by C. The manuscript includes chants for the Proper of the Time (Palm Sunday to Eve of Pentecost) as well as Masses and interpolated Offices for the Proper of the Time and Proper of the Saints, ending with an isolated sequence and invitatory. Of the 148 folios, ff. 1r–115v have Arabic foliation with red ink, whereas the latter folios have later added Roman foliation in black ink (ff. Ir–XXXIIIv). The inventory continues the Arabic numbering from 116r–148v rather than switching to the Roman foliation, but the Roman numbering is included in the Extra Field (any Roman numbering that is difficult to discern is indicated in square brackets, as in [1]). There is evidence of a different copyist’s hand on ff. 146v–148v for the sequence 'Victimae paschali laudes' and the invitatory for the Transfiguration 'Summum regem gloriae' (fragmented). There are three lacunae: at 114v within Vigilia Pentecostes; 115r at the end of Vigilia Pentecostes and before a brief section of Mass Ordinary chants (Credo, Kyrie); and at 145v with a missing Magnificat antiphon for the feast of Joachim and before the concluding folios in a different hand.  The inventory includes manuscript abbreviations in the 'source spelling' field. Abbreviated letters are indicated using a circumflex (ex: ê). As such, the circumflex indicates the presence of an abbreviation, but not the specific abbreviatory mark. Consultation with the manuscript images can confirm which abbreviatory mark was employed by the scribe. The differentiae for the introit verses and antiphons are identified by differentia final and a sequentially-ordered numeral (ex: E1, E2). Variant versions of differentiae receive a letter suffix (ex: E1a, E2a). There is one fully notated invitatory tone: PA at 128v for Exspectationis BMV (an incipit only version occurs at 122v for Exaltatio Crucis). This fragmented Gradual is part of a collection of thirty-eight liturgical manuscripts within the collection of the Church of San Francisco in Quito, including fifteen antiphonaries, four graduals, eight hymnals, ten psalters, and one ritual (see Estévez Monagas, 2019). Although much work has been done to address church music in Quito (including by American musicologist Robert M. Stevenson and Spanish musicologist Alejandro Massó), the plainchant manuscripts of Quito are an emerging area of research, with the inventory for EC-Qsf 18P16 being the first published inventory of a plainchant volume from an Ecuadorian church (released online on the Cantus Database in February 2021, after creation during 2017-19 and proofreading in 2020).

title: Montréal, McGill University - Rare Books and Special Collections - Manuscript Collection, MS Medieval 0087
description: Antiphonal leaf, probably German and late 15th or early 16th century. The music notation is square on a four-line black staff; the f-clef is a typical German “Hufnagel” style clef, and occasionally appears alongside the c clef on the same staff. The music was apparently corrected or altered, possibly to give rhythmic indications: occasional isolated diamond-shaped notes appear, and in several places tails have been added, or the shape of the pes changed so that the second note is to the right of the first.  Script is Northern Textualis Formata, sharply pointed, with well defined feet on the minims, even hairlines at the tops of minims, and some clubbed ascenders.  Decorated with fine, elaborate curling vines in the margin, delicately shaded in a pale green-rose-blue-gold colour palette. Several identifiable bird species (magpie, woodpecker, heron) are depicted in the foliage.A large initial red F sits inside a trompe-l’oeuil frame on a black and gold background, textured with more foliage. The colours, naturalism, and interest in texture are reminiscent of German work of the later 15th century (a dating and provenance also supported by the script); the square music notation, rather than Hufnagel,  might suggest a geographic placing to the north or west (near Belgium or the Netherlands).  Compare the similar decoration style, also with square notation, used in a fragmented German antiphoner at the Victoria and Albert:https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O1028908/manuscript-cutting/?carousel-image=2023NP1601https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O87087/manuscript-cutting-unknown/) On the “frame” of the illuminated F, several Arabic numbers are visible; possibly this is a date (1500). Chants for Ambrose (or another confessor) in Paschaltide, for a single martyr in Paschaltide, and for several martyrs in Paschaltide.  (The McGill library description identifies this source as Spanish, but it is more likely German as described above.)

title: Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS. Canon. Liturg. 202
description: A note written on fol. 1v in 1361 by a Tuscan priest (as transcribed by van Dijk) indicates that the book was in Lombardy by the fourteenth century:Nota quod ego presbiter Tuscanus canonicus ecclesie sancti Petri et capellanus de Sundrio accepi librum istum mutuo ab ecclesia sancti Petri. submillesimo.ccc.lxj indict.xiij.Frere’s suggestion of a connection to the Dominican Order has not been confirmed. Contributing to the suggestion of south German provenance are the Offices of Florian and Gall. On page 309 of Young (1967), there is an edition of the text of the Easter play (beginning Quis revolvit) and on page 690, the rubric describing the ceremony of the Visitatio Sepulchri (72v-73r). The latter is also found on page 900 of Young’s The Harrowing of Hell, along with an edition of the rubric describing of the Elevatio Crucis (71v).This manuscript contains some examples of multiple Offices or parts of Offices for individual liturgical occasions. Examples occur for the feasts of St. Stephen and St. John the Evangelist (alternate antiphons for the three nocturns of Matins are given before a complete Matins office), for the Common of Many Martyrs (an alternate set of antiphons for Lauds is given) and for the summer historia De Regum. In this last case, the first of the ferial antiphons (and by extension, probably the entire set) are indicated as an alternative under the rubric “alio modo.”Modes for responsories are provisional; they are being proposed according to an analysis of the neume patterns found in responsory verses and the modal designations of corresponding responsories in other sources represented in the database. This analysis has demonstrated that the standard verse tones are consistently represented within these leaves by neume patterns distinctive for each mode. Because of their provisional nature, all mode numbers for responsories in the file are followed by a question mark. Where there is any ambiguity (such as in cases where a non-standard tone is given for a verse or where the verse cannot be sufficiently read), a mode has not been assigned.

title: Wolfenbüttel, Herzog August Bibliothek, Cod. Guelf. 28 Helmst. (Heinemann-Nr. 31)
description: This antiphoner was written for the female Augustinian chapter of canonesses, St. Vitus in Hilwartshausen. It may have been paired with D-W 29 Helmst. (Heinemann 32), as the contents are complementary. The manuscript was given to the Fritzlar library by Wilhelm von Lysfelt, and transferred from Fritzlar to Wolfenbüttel in 1587.  Physical Description: Parchment leaves. Covers of pigskin over wood binding. The manuscript has coloured initials with garnet ornaments (leaves and flowers) on ff. 1r, 6r, 19r, 28r, 57r, 124r, 180r, and 202v. Other initials are in red, blue, and black. Modern foliation (I to CXCI) in red ink on ff. 28-219. Differentiae are indicated by their last note and an arbitrarily-assigned number (e.g., G1, D1, E1, etc.). This manuscript source was previously identified in the Cantus Database as #31, as listed in the manuscript catalogue of Otto von Heinemann.

title: Wolfenbüttel, Herzog August Bibliothek, Cod. Guelf. 29 Helmst. (Heinemann-Nr. 32)
description: The inscription of the initial on f. 135v indicates that the manuscript was from a nunnery, possibly the female Augustinian chapter of canonesses, St. Vitus in Hilwartshausen. It may have been paired with D-W 28 Helmst. (Heinemann 31), as the contents are complementary. The manuscript was given to the Fritzlar library by Wilhelm von Lysfelt, and transferred from Fritzlar to Wolfenbüttel in 1587. Physical Description: Parchment leaves. Covers of pigskin over wood binding. The manuscript includes decorated, coloured initials in blue, red, green, and black on ff. 1r, 46r, 14v, 135v, 141r, and 147v. Other initials are in red, blue, and black. Blue-red fleuronnée initials on ff. 5r, 9v, 16v, and 88v. Differentiae are indexed by their last note and an arbitrarily-assigned number (e.g., G1, D1, E1, etc.). This manuscript source was previously identified in the.Cantus Database as #32, as listed in the manuscript catalogue of Otto von Heinemann.

title: E-H (Huesca) Ms. 9
description: Breviary from Huesca. Pars tertia.     Shelf-mark: Ms. 9 (ant. 25).     Date: twelfth century ex. (Durán); twelfth century ex.- thirteenth century in. (Garrigosa); thirteenth century (Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini).     Provenance: Huesca.     Physical description: Third volume of a Breviary divided into three volumes (mss. 7, 8 and 9). 286 ff.: parchment; 450 x 315 mm, text block 290 x 210 mm. Modern foliation with Arabic numerals in pencil in the upper right-hand margin of the recto. Wood binding, the front cover is missing.     Layout of the script: two-column layout with an average of 25 lines of text.     State of conservation: An overall good conservation.     Decoration: Initials in green, blue and red, with filigree work.     Musical notation: Aquitanian on drypoint lines.     Content summary: it contains the offices of the sanctorale, from Saint Nicholas to the feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle, the office of the Dedication of a Church, the Common of Saints and the office of the Dead, with intercalated proses and verbetas (responsorial prosulas). On the last folio (f. 286r) the scribe wrote these Leonine verses: Pennula scriptoris requiescat fessa laboris. Qui dedit a et o laus et gloria Christo. Amen.                 Breviarium oscense. Pars tertia     Signatura: Ms. 9 (ant. 25)     Datación: siglo XII ex. (Durán); siglos XII ex.-XIII in. (Garrigosa); siglo XIII (Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini)     Procedencia: Huesca     Descripción física: tomo III de un Breviario repartido en 3 tomos (mss. 7, 8 y 9). 286 ff.: pergamino; 450 x 315 mm, caja de 290 x 210 mm. Foliación moderna con numeración arábiga a lápiz en el margen superior derecho del recto. Encuadernación en madera, le falta la cubierta anterior.     Disposición de la escritura: texto distribuido a 2 columnas con un promedio de 25 líneas de texto.     Estado de conservación: Buena conservación en general.     Decoración: Iniciales en verde, azul y rojo, afiligranadas.     Notación musical: Aquitana sobre línea a punta seca.     Resumen del contenido: Contiene los oficios del santoral, desde San Nicolás hasta la fiesta de San Andrés Apóstol, el oficio de la dedicación de la iglesia, común de los santos y oficio de difuntos, con prosas intercaladas y verbetas. En el último folio (f. 286r) el copista escribió estos versos leoninos: Pennula scriptoris requiescat fessa laboris. Qui dedit a et o laus et gloria Christo. Amen.

title: E-H (Huesca) Ms. 7
description: Breviary from Huesca. Pars prior.     Shelf-mark: Ms. 7 (ant. 5).     Date: twelfth century ex. (Durán); twelfth century ex. and thirteenth century in. (Garrigosa); thirteenth century (Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini).     Provenance: Huesca.     Physical description: volume I of a Breviary divided into three volumes (mss. 7, 8 and 9). 194 ff.: parchment ; 485 x 340 mm (Durán / Garrigosa / Janini), 485 x 327 mm (Fdez. de la Cuesta), text block 310 x 240 mm. Modern foliation with Arabic numerals in pencil in the upper right-hand margin of the recto. Binding with wood.      Layout of the script: two-column layout with an average of 25 lines of text.     State of conservation: an overall good conservation.     Decoration: initials in green, red and blue, with filigree work.     Musical notation: Aquitanian on drypoint lines.     Content summary: it contains the Proper of Time with intercalated prose, from the first Sunday of Advent to Holy Saturday; the Song of the Sibyl (ff. 44v-45); gospels of the genealogies according to Saint Matthew (f. 53) and Saint Luke (f. 75v-75), as well as the Lamentations of Jeremiah (f. 186v).                 Breviarium oscense. Pars prior.     Signatura: Ms. 7 (ant. 5).     Datación: siglo XII ex. (Durán); siglos XII ex.-XIII in. (Garrigosa); siglo XIII (Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini).     Procedencia: Huesca.     Descripción física: tomo I de un Breviario repartido en 3 tomos (mss. 7, 8 y 9). 194 ff.: pergamino; 485 x 340 mm (Durán / Garrigosa / Janini), 485 x 327 mm (Fdez. de la Cuesta), caja de 310 x 240 mm. Foliación moderna con numeración arábiga a lápiz en el margen superior derecho del recto. Encuadernación en madera.     Disposición de la escritura: texto distribuido a 2 columnas con un promedio de 25 líneas de texto.     Estado de conservación: Buena conservación en general.     Decoración: Iniciales en verde, azul y rojo, afiligranadas.     Notación musical: Aquitana sobre línea a punta seca.     Resumen del contenido: Contiene el propio del tiempo con prosas intercaladas, desde el Domingo I de Adviento hasta el Sábado Santo, Canto de la Sibila (ff. 44v-45), evangelios de las genealogías según san Mateo (f. 53) y san Lucas (f. 75v-75), así como las lamentaciones de Jeremías (f. 186v).

title: E-H (Huesca) Ms. 8

Content summary: it contains the Proper of Time with with intercalated proses and verbetas (responsorial prosulas), from Resurrection Sunday to the twenty-sixth Sunday after Pentecost.                 Breviarium oscense. Pars altera.     Signatura: Ms. 8 (ant. 6).     Datación: siglo XII ex. (Durán); siglos XII ex.-XIII in. (Garrigosa); siglo XIII (Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini).     Procedencia: Huesca.     Descripción física: tomo II de un Breviario repartido en 3 tomos (mss. 7, 8 y 9). 157 ff.: pergamino; 425 x 315 mm (Durán / Garrigosa / Janini), 425 x 340 mm (Fdez. de la Cuesta), caja de 280 x 220 mm. Foliación moderna con numeración arábiga a lápiz en el margen superior derecho del recto. Encuadernación en madera.     Disposición de la escritura: texto distribuido a 2 columnas con un promedio de 25 líneas de texto.     Estado de conservación: Buena conservación en general con algunos folios muy deteriorados.     Decoración: Iniciales en verde, azul y rojo, afiligranadas.     Notación musical: Aquitana sobre línea a punta seca.
