title: Vorau, Stiftsbibliothek, 287 (olim XXIX)
description: The texts of a number of unusual Offices not recorded in Hesbert's Corpus Antiphonalium Officii have already been edited in Analecta Hymnica: Dorothy (vol. 5, 56); Margaret (vol. 28, 3); Eustace (vol. 26, 15); Elizabeth of Hungary (vol. 25, 90); Catherine (vol. 26, 69); Martha (vol. 28, 45); Barbara (vol. 25, 121); Immaculate Conception (vol. 5, 47); Juliana (vol. 26, 184); Anne (vol. 5, 110); Holy Lance (vol. 5, 35); Acacius and Companions (vol. 5, 91). Many texts are not included in Analecta Hymnica, including Corpus Christi (the version attributed to Thomas Aquinas), Augustine, the Beheading of John the Baptist, the 11,000 Virgins, and Thomas the Apostle. Of these five Offices, only that for Corpus Christi may be found in Hughes, LMLO.Two special items in the manuscript are of interest but were not indexed in our file: the tonary, with antiphons whose melismas outline each of the eight modes (ff. 285v-286v); canticle tones which have been notated to the first verse of both Magnificat and Benedictus canticles, in all eight modes (ff. 286v-288r).In addition to Mass Alleluias in second Vespers in Easter week, the manuscript includes Alleluias for Barbara (304v01), Immaculate Conception (310v02), Anne (320r01), and Acacius and Companions (336r03). That for Barbara (Alleluia O beata Barbara deo) was transcribed from Vorau 287 in Karlheinz Schlager, ed., Alleluia-Melodien, 2 vols., Monumenta Monodica Medii Aevi 7-8 (Kassel: Baerenreiter, 1968, 1987), 2: 301. There are also three sequences, for Immaculate Conception (O consolatrix pauperum, 310v03), Anne (Caeli regem attollamus, 319v01), and a non-specific Marian sequence (Gaude virgo gratiosa, 320v06).Some paleographical details of the manuscript posed problems for the indexers. The numerous errors of the text scribe--insertions, omissions, wrong words--have been carefully corrected in marginal and interlinear annotations, apparently by the music scribe. In cases that affected the incipit to be recorded in the file, the text was always entered with these corrections. The system of differentiae also appears to have been implemented by at least two scribes, either contemporaneously or at different times. Nearly all differentiae listed in the tonary occur throughout the manuscript in two to five variations (some are found only in the tonary). Two-digit differentia numbers reflect this problem: an Arabic number indicates the basic differentia with a lower case letter for the variation (if no variation was observed, only an Arabic number was used).

title: Aberystwyth, Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru (National Library of Wales), 20541 E
description: One group of folios near the end of the manuscript is misbound. The correct order is as follows: 236, 238, 237, 240, 239, 241. In the index, these folios have been renumbered in order to restore the correct order of chants; sorting on the numbers in the Marginalia field will restore the misbound order of the folios in the manuscript. The ordering of these folios is also corrected in the facsimile reproduction of the Penpont Antiphoner. There is a detailed codicological analysis of the manuscript in the introduction to that work.The numbering of the differentiae in this index follows that of the Sarum Tonale (published by Frere in The Use of Sarum). In it, as here, the tonus peregrinus is assigned to mode 8 differentia 5. Six of the differentiae in the Penpont antiphoner are indicated by pitches or neumations that are slightly different from those in the Sarum Tonale: these are 1.8, 2.2, 3.2, 3.3, 3.5, and 4.2. In addition, two differentiae (4.9 and 7.7) that appear in the Sarum Tonale are lacking in the Penpont antiphoner. One differentia in Penpont, 2.3, appears to be a variant of either 2.1 or 2.2, but it is impossible to determine which. This differentia is not in the Sarum Tonale.

title: Stuttgart, Württembergische Landesbibliothek, HB.I.55
description: Stuttgart HB.I.55 was used at the Abbey of Weingarten, a Benedictine house in Wuerttemberg, Germany. Although it was originally founded some time after the year 934 as a house for women religious, the nuns of Weingarten moved to Altomuenster in Freising in 1056, and the monks of Altomuenster moved to Weingarten. Under Welf IV and his wife Judith, Weingarten became an imperial abbey; and after 1088 it followed the customs of Hirsau. The abbey was suppressed in 1803 and restored in 1922. The contents of Stuttgart HB.I.55 are misbound: the table below indicates their correct sequence. 5r-5v: Advent I 2r-3v: Advent I to Advent II 6r-7v: Advent II to Advent III 4r-4v: Advent III lacuna 8r-15v: Lucy to Christmas lacuna 16r-21v: John the Evangelist to Epiphany lacuna 22r-84v: Epiphany to Easter Monday 86r-100v: Easter Monday to Ascension 85r-85v: Ascension 101r-126v: Pentecost to Laurence lacuna 127r-190v: Assumption to Benedict In addition to being misbound and having four lacunae, the manuscript contains two leaves (55 and 157) that have numbers that are repeated on the leaves that follow them: there are two leaves marked 55 and two marked 157. In each instance the recto of the second of the pair of leaves is referred to in the index not as r but as w; and x is used in place of v for the verso. This enables them to be distinguished from the leaves that precede them; and when the file is sorted on folio number (including r, v, w, and x,) the order of folios in the source is preserved. The manuscript is notated in non-diastematic neumes, which makes the identification of mode difficult in many instances. Wherever possible the series of neumes used to notate the verses of responsories have been matched with modal formulas, and the modes of those responsories thus identified. It has also been possible to identify the modes of many antiphons in the index. The manuscript employs two different systems for specifying differentiae: neumes and tonary letters. The neumes appear in the outer margins of the openings, the tonary letters in the inner margins. The index records the tonary letter or letters (if present) in an extra field to reflect what appears to be signified by the differentiae given in neumes. These designations are based on the incomplete tonary at the end of the manuscript; tonary letters have been assigned arbitrarily to the differentiae of the first three modes.Stuttgart HB.I.55 contains several CAO Offices that are known in relatively limited regions (i.e., Gregory, Mary Magdalene, Afra, and Gall) but contains only two Offices not found in CAO, those for King Oswald and Benedict. The text of the former is edited in Analecta hymnica, vol. 13, pp. 209-12, and the text of the latter is also in Analecta hymnica vol. 25, pp. 145-9.All chants not found in CAO have been assigned an arbitrary number prefixed by wei.

title: Worcester, Cathedral - Music Library, F. 160 (olim 1247) (facsimile)
description: The manuscript Worcester F.160 contains a monastic antiphoner, processional, calendar, psalter, hymnal, collectarium, tonary, kyriale, gradual and a fragmentary proser; the antiphoner and processional were reproduced in facsimile in Paleographie musicale 12 (Tournai: Desclee, 1922). The volume includes a tonary of the antiphons that was drawn up by Laurentia McLachlan, who also wrote the introduction.The Cantus inventory exists in two forms. One includes all the chants in the antiphoner, processional, and hymnal, including the Offices of the Visitation of Mary and Corpus Christi, which were added in the fourteenth century. (Though not included in the facsimile edition, these two Offices are discussed in the introduction to it.) The location numbers in this version of the index are the folios of the manuscript. A second version of the index includes only the chants of the antiphoner and this version's location numbers are the pages of the facsimile edition. In the index with the facsimile page numbers, the folio numbers of the manuscript are found in the Addendum field, and likewise in the version with the manuscript folio numbers, the Addendum field contains the facsimile pages.A number of rare Offices for Anglo-Saxon saints occur in Worcester F.160, namely Cuthbert, Dunstan, Oswald, and Wulfstan; texts for the antiphons in Cuthbert's Office may be found in Analecta hymnica, vol. 13, p. 102. (It should be noted that the Analecta hymnica edition follows a source that presents the secular cursus, so not all the Worcester antiphons are to be found in it.) The Offices for Cuthbert and Wulfstan are briefly discussed by Andrew Hughes in British Rhymed Offices: A Catalogue and Commentary in Music in the Medieval English Liturgy, Susan Rankin and David Hiley, eds. (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1993), pp. 257 and 279f, respectively. The Office for Corpus Christi also appears in Arras 893. Differentiae follow the numbering of the tonary of the manuscript (as prepared for the facsimile edition) with one important modification: certain differentiae occur both with and without liquescent notes, and these distinctions were not taken into account by the compiler of the tonary. However, they are reflected in the Cantus inventory by an a added to differentiae with liquescent notes. The differentia labelled 8.5 in the tonary (the tonus peregrinus) is labelled 8 P in the Cantus inventory.About the Invitatory tones of Worcester F.160Invitatory tones are represented in Worcester F.160 in two different ways. All of the tones are written out in full on ff. 96r-99v (pp. 192-99 of the facsimile edition); elsewhere in the source they are referred to only by incipit. The repertory of thirteen invitatory tones includes many standard ones: 2 for some mode-2 invitatory antiphons; FE for use in the ferial Office; CH for Christmas and Epiphany; the tone NE; 3 for a small number of mode-3 antiphons; BL for antiphons of mode 2 or mode 4; as well as the tones named 5 and 7.Worcester F.160 does record one unusual tone, labelled WR, which is used throughout the liturgical year, in both temporale and sanctorale. Although rarely encountered, this tone is not unique to Worcester; it appears in various other sources, even in Toledo 44.1 (though there only as an incipit).The invitatory tones labelled PA and IN, usually associated with Paschal time and the feast of the Holy Innocents respectively, occur in Worcester, but each also has a variant labelled PX or IX. These four tones all occur at the end of the series (98v-99r), and may indicate some confusion on the part of the scribe: the tone IN is assigned to Easter Sunday; the tone IN was originally assigned to Easter Monday, erased, and the PX tone added by a later hand; and an invitatory antiphon sung during Pentecost week (77r; p. 154) is followed by the incipits for the IN, PX, and PA tones. (The PA tone incipit appears only twice, here and after the invitatory antiphon for the feast of Wulfstan.)

title: Köln, Erzbischöfliche Diözesan- und Dombibliothek, 215
description: The manuscript likely originated in a Benedictine male monastery in the diocese of Würzburg before coming to the Cologne Cathedral by the fourteenth century. The inclusion of chants for St. Burchard, the first bishop of Würzburg (ff. 135v-136r), and St. Kilian (ff. 118r-120v) suggest that the manuscript was used and/or created in the diocese of Würzburg. The predominantly red and green miniatures (ff. 82v, 83r, and 88v) were not completed at the same time or place as the text and neumation. The miniatures depict the betrayal of Christ by Judas; the teachings of Christ; and scenes from the resurrection of Christ, respectively. They were completed earlier in Liège(?) at the end of the eleventh century and inserted into the manuscript. They are thought to be from Liège owing to the similar ornamentation style in Ms. 9369-9370 in the Royal Library of Belgium, a late-eleventh century MS from the Abbey of Saint Laurent in Liège. In the late-thirteenth century, a tonary (ff. 209v-212r) in diastematic neumes was added to the manuscript, organized by mode.By the fourteenth century, the manuscript had moved to the Cologne Cathedral, as indicated by an annotation on f. 206r that refers to the Archbishop Wilhelm of Gennep (1349-1362): “Wilhelmus Dei gratia sancta Coloniensis ecclesiae.” Physical Description: Parchment leaves. Rebound in the mid-eighteenth century with paper over cardboard. The manuscript includes eighteen ornamented text initials (e.g. 11r) and three full-page colour miniatures (ff. 82v, 83r, and 88v). In addition to the antiphoner (ff. 10v-209r), the manuscript also contains a liturgical kalendar (ff. 1r-6r) for every month except January; a tonary (209v-212r) that was added in the late-thirteenth century); a hymnary (ff. 212-216v); and a psalter, cantica, and orations (ff. 217r-279r). The leaves are numbered in a later hand in pencil in the upper right-hand corner of each recto side. The miniatures (ff. 82v, 83r, and 88v) were likely completed in the Maas region, near Liège, at the end of the eleventh century; the text and neumes date from the beginning of the twelfth century; and the tonary (ff. 209v-212r) was added in the late-thirteenth century. Differentiae in this manuscript are indicated by letters in the margins which may correspond with the differentiae in the tonary, but there are no clear indications of how the two systems correlate with each other. Those provided in the tonary are transcribed in the differentia table.

title: Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS. Laud Misc. 284
description: The manuscript was likely written in Würzburg between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries, possibly at the Domstift St Kilian. It is in three parts: ff. 1-118, a choir breviary, likely made up from an antiphonal from the twelfth to the fourteenth centuries; ff. 119-268, a lectionary, thirteenth to fourteenth centuries; and ff. 269-272, additions, fourteenth century. The bastarda script used in the catchwords of the second and third parts suggest that these two parts, possibly all three, were combined in the fifteenth century. The Abbey of the Holy Redeemer, or St Kilian’s, was a male order Benedictine monastery formed c. 745 by Burchard. The monks had also had control over the Würzburg Cathedral and cathedral school until 786, when Bishop Berowelf of Würzburg replaced the monks with canons and formed the Domstift, the collegiate institution that provided a home for the cathedral chapter. The Domstift was secularized in 1803. MS. Laud Misc. 284 was donated to the Bodleian Library, Oxford in 1639 by Archbishop William Laud (1573-1645), the Archbishop of Canterbury, as part of a group of over 1200 manuscripts that he donated between 1635 and 1641. Many of these manuscripts, like 284, were originally from Würzburg. Many of the Laud’s manuscripts were given to him by Thomas Howard (1585-1646), the fourteenth earl of Arundel, acquired from Germany during the Thirty Years’ War (1618-1648). The manuscript is written on vellum. The manuscript was rebound in the seventeenth century for Laud with brown tanned calf-skin over laminated pulpboard and three endleaves (two paper and one parchment). Laud’s armorial centrepiece, tooled in gold, is on the binding. The front flyleaf includes a fragment of a notarial instrument by Conrad of Nördlingen, diocese of Augsburg, relating to a lawsuit involving the Dean and Chapter of Würzburg. The folios are numbered in a modern, nineteenth-century hand in pencil, and end leaves in a different, twentieth-century hand. The differentiae are indicated by letters in the margins of the manuscript, which have been transcribed in the differentiae column of the index. The manuscript does not include a tonary to indicate the associated formulas for these letters.

title: Zutphen, Stadsarchief en Stedelijke Bibliotheek, 6
description: Some Offices are found in the volumes of Analecta hymnica: Presentation of Mary, in Analecta hymnica vol. 24, pp. 76-80; Holy Lance, partly in Analecta hymnica vol. 5, pp. 35-36, cf. Vorau (A-VOR 287); Visitation of Mary, in Analecta hymnica vol. 24, pp. 89-94; Anna, partly in Analecta hymnica vol. 5, pp. 115-117; Gudula - The Office from the Brussels Gudula Church, partly in Analecta hymnica vol. 26, pp. 78-79; Elizabeth of Hungary, in Analecta hymnica vol. 25, pp. 253-258, cf. Cambrai (F-CA 38); Francis of Assisi, in Analecta hymnica vol. 5, pp. 175-178, cf. Budapest (H-Bu lat. 118, 119, 121, 122); Justus, in Analecta hymnica vol. 55, pp. 404-408.Many of the Offices in the 16th-century portion of the manuscript received their place in the Zutphen liturgy in the later Middle Ages. The manuscript contains an Office of Gudula, partly known from sources of Brussels. A church was dedicated to this saint in the village of Lochem, a church under the control of the Zutphen chapter. The Justus Office reflects veneration for Justus during the 15th century, a veneration which also led to the founding of a Confraternity for Ewald and Justus in 1454. Relics of Justus of Beauvais had been preserved in Zutphen since at least the 14th century; and an additional relic for the saint was brought by the Franciscans when they established themselves in Zutphen, around 1450. The settling of the Franciscans at this time also explains the occurrence of a Francis Office in the later additions to the MS. Other relics were kept in Zutphen as well, including the bones of Bartholomew and some skulls of the 11, 000 virgins. These relics were taken out of Zutphen during the religious troubles at the end of the 16th century and brought to Antwerp.Among the 15th century portions of the manuscript we find:An Office for Walburga, patron saint of the church. This Office is a compilation of chants, written originally for Walburga or for other female saints (some chants are found in the Office of Gertrudis of Nivelles, Analecta hymnica vol. 26, pp. 60-63).The relatively extended Office for Margaret in the 15th century part of the MS (in prose; with psalm quotations in some of the chants; not in Analecta hynnica or LMLO) can perhaps be explained by the fact that in St. Walburga's was a Margaret chapel; this was the chapel of the counts of Zutphen.The Bartholomew Office is not in Analecta hymnica; some chants can be found in LMLO (BA84 and BA85).In the Zutphen tradition, some saints are celebrated on idiosyncratic dates. According to all Zutphen sources, the translation of Walburga's relics to Eichstätt is celebrated on 24 September, while in Eichstätt (where she is buried together with her brother) it is celebrated on 12 October. The translation of Gudula is in Zutphen on 8 October, but in Brussels (where her relics were brought in the 11th century and where her Office originated) on 6 July. Justus of Beauvais is celebrated in Zutphen on 11 October, though his feast is traditionally 18 October. Apparently Justus of Beauvais was confused with Justus of Arras.Although Zutphen is now a relatively small city in the east of the Netherlands, it was a flourishing town during the Middle Ages, the residence of the counts of both Zutphen and the county (from 1339 onwards duchy) Gelre.The chapter of Zutphen was founded in the 11th century, and consisted of a provost and 12 canons; there were 11-16 vicars and in 15th-century documents 3 chorisocii are mentioned. In addition, there were also schoolboys. The church is connected with the famous Librije, a unique late medieval library built adjacent to the church.The presence of an organ is known from the first half of the 15th century onwards. No traces of polyphonic vocal music are known.Most of the books and documents of the chapter are kept in the Municipal Archive (the Stadsarchief or Gemeentelijk Archief Zutphen). Some are in the Librije or elsewhere.Other sources for the Zutphen Office are:Breviarium festivum (Brussels, Bibl. Bollandistes, ms 680), prepared ca. 1470 (without notation).Two choir books (Zutphen, GAZ, ms 2 and Zutphen, Librije, ms 6), dating from the 2nd half of the 15th century, partly early 16th century, each containing a limited number of Offices, and some sequences. The books are identical and apparently meant for both sides of the choir.A small 15th century book with the responsoria brevia (Zutphen, Librije, ms 5)For the Mass, unnoted missals have generally survived; only some sequences (e.g. for Walburga) are preserved with music.In the 2nd half of the 16th century, during the religious troubles, Zutphen came under Protestant control. From that time onwards the Catholic religion was forbidden in the northern part of the Netherlands. Although some chapters (e.g. the Utrecht chapters) managed to continue until the end of the 18th century, the Zutphen chapter was disbanded around 1600.

title: Karlsruhe, Badische Landesbibliothek - Musiksammlung, Aug. LX
description: Karlsruhe Aug. LX presents several challenges to the researcher. It is written in six different hands and seven notational styles spanning five centuries. A brief overview is provided below:	1: late 12th-century Carolingian minuscule	2: an early 13th-century hand on ff. 261r-262v	3: a mid-13th-century Gothic minuscule (ff. 225v-230r--the added Offices of Elizabeth of Hungary and Catherine of Alexandria)	4: a mid-15th-century hand (the added material on ff. 104r-144)	5: 15th-century Gothic minuscule (ff. 133v-240v)	6: 15th-century Humanist hand (140v) 	Karl Hain describes the characteristics of each hand in his Ein musikalischer Palimpsest, pp. 21-9; his discussion of the different notations, describing exactly where they are used in the manuscript, can be found on pp. 30-69. The seven types of notations he describes are the following:	1: a 12th-century South-German notation with red F-line and yellow C-line similar to the one found in Graz 807 (ff. 82v and 225v-227v)	2: German notation with red F-line and yellow C-line similar to the onle found in GB-Lbl-B. Add. 24680 and B-Br-2034 (ff. 219v-221r)	3: German notation on four-line staff (223r)	4: German notation (ff. 22r, 129v, 223v-224v, 231r, 233v)	5: Hufnagel notation on four-line staff, found anywhere when not otherwise specified	6: a 15th-century notation on five-line staff, found in the interpolated material (ff. 1r [211]-30v [270])        7: Square notation on red four-line staff (ff. 191r-193r) 	Chants are often written in a haphazard manner: for example, the ending of the antiphon “O clavis David et sceptrum” (14v) is written four lines above where it is begun. This is especially prevalent among verses to responsories (e.g., see ff. 44v, 45r, 65v, 68v, 76r, 170r, 204r, 212v). An extreme example of this is the verse “Averte oculos meos ne videant,” which is begun on 103v but is continued on 142r. 	The full texts of the Offices of Elizabeth of Hungary and Catherine of Alexandria can be found in Analecta hymnica, vol. 25, pp. 253-8, and vol. 26, pp. 212-5, respectively. The rhymed Office for Benedict appears full in Analecta hymnica, vol. 25, pp. 145-9. 	Differentiae are not notated in Karlsruhe Aug. LX; instead, the mode and differentia of many of the antiphons are indicated by letters (a vowel followed by a consonant). Unfortunately, some of the differentiae appear to have been trimmed off.Another challenging aspect of this manuscript concerns the multiple sets of folio numbers. The records here correspond to the folio numbering used by the Badische Landesbibliothek in their digital images (posted to the library website in 2015). The Cantus Database records were edited during the summer of 2015; for example, the former fol. 004r is the new fol. 002r, old 004v = new 002v, etc.

title: B-Br (Bruselas) IV/473
description: Physical description: 151 ff.; rectangular format and vertical orientation with dimensions 215 x 151 mm. Written on parchment the manuscript has been bound in 19 fascicles with the following scheme of booklets: IV (8) + IV (16) + IV (24) + IV (32) + IV (40) + IV (48) + IV (56) + IV (64) + IV (72) + IV (80) + IV (88) + IV (96) + IV (104) + IV (112) + IV (120) + IV (128) + IV (136) + IV (144) + III (150). At the end of the manuscript there are two folios of guards marked A and B with later handwriting. They contain a series of annotations as an index to some of the incipits. The main foliation is in red Roman numerals, while a later foliation in Arabic numerals can be found in the upper margin of the straight folios. Arrangement of the writing: In general, it has been written as a line, with two sections with different typesetting: ff. 1 - 144 (cycles of the vesperal time and saints) with six typesettings per page and ff. 145 - 149 (litany of saints) with eighteen textual lines. However, exceptions can be found such as f. 143v with only three pautados, f. 144r blank, f. 144v with four pautados or f. 149v with one textual line and one musical line. Condition: Some damage (mutilations), but generally in good condition. Textual script: Bookplate Gothic script. Musical notation: Square notation in black over a tetradrachm in red ink, except for two pieces that were added later. The first, Sicut cervus desiderat, is found on f. 144v with a five-line pattern in black ink, and the second, on f. 149v, the Pueri Hebreorum is added over the recticial lines. Decoration: There are three types of initials. The first is a musical-textual line, coloured in red or blue ink; it begins each piece. The second is of a broken type, in black ink; they function as the first letter of the internal parts of each piece. The third type has a tertiary structural function, in red or blue ink. They are of the square type and appear as initials of verses and initials in litanies. Dating: From the Chapter Library of Saragossa (E-Zs). It is dated to the end of the 14th century with the content of a responsorial processional. Taking into account the arrangement, we can say that it is a responsorial processional, table IV of Michel Huglo, Les manuscrits du processional (p. 48*). Descripción física: 151 ff.; Formato rectangular y orientación vertical con las dimensiones 215 x 151 mm. Escrito sobre pergamino el manuscrito ha sido encuadernado en 19 fascículos con el siguiente esquema de cuadernillos: IV (8) + IV (16) + IV (24) + IV (32) + IV (40) + IV (48) + IV (56) + IV (64) + IV (72) + IV (80) + IV (88) + IV (96) + IV (104) + IV (112) + IV (120) + IV (128) + IV (136) + IV (144) + III (150). Al final del manuscrito se pueden encontrar dos folios de guarda marcadas como A y B con escritura más tardía. Presentan una serie de anotaciones a modo de índice sobre algunos íncipits. Foliación principal en números romanos de color rojo, mientras se puede encontrar una más tardía realizada en números arábigos en el margen superior de los folios rectos. Disposición de la escritura: En general se ha realizado a línea tirada contando con dos secciones con diferente pautado: ff. 1 – 144 (ciclos del tiempo vesperal y santos) con seis pautados por página y ff. 145 – 149 (letanía de los santos) con dieciocho líneas textuales. Sin embargo, se pueden encontrar excepciones como en el f. 143v con solo tres pautados, el f. 144r en blanco, el f. 144v con cuatro pautados o el f. 149v con una línea textual y una musical. Estado de conservación: Presenta algunos daños (mutilaciones), pero en general está en buen estado. Escritura textual: Letra gótica libraria. Notación musical: Notación cuadrada en negro sobre un tetragrama en tinta roja, excepto dos piezas que fueron añadidas posteriormente. La primera es Sicut cervus desiderat se encuentra en el f. 144v con un pautado en tinta negra con cinco líneas y la segunda, en el f. 149v se añade el Pueri Hebreorum sobre las líneas rectices. Decoración: Presenta tres tipos de iniciales. El primero ocupa una línea músico-textual, coloreada en tinta roja o azul; da comienzo a cada pieza. El segundo es de tipo quebrado, en tinta de color negro; funcionan como primera letra de las partes internas de cada pieza. El tercer tipo tienen función estructural terciaria, en tinta de color rojo o azul. Son de tipo cuadrado y aparecen como iniciales de los versículos e iniciales en las letanías. Datación: Procedente de la Biblioteca Capitular de Zaragoza (E-Zs). Se data finales del siglo XIV con contenido de un procesional responsorial. Teniendo en cuenta la ordenación se puede concretar que es un procesional responsorial, tabla IV de Michel Huglo, Les manuscrits du processional (p. 48*).

title: E-BAR (Barbastro) 95
description: Physical description: 139 ff.; rectangular format and oriented vertically with dimensions 225 x 155 x 55 mm. Written on parchment, the manuscript has been bound in 18 fascicles with the following pattern of booklets: IV (8) + IV (16) + IV (24) + IV (32) + IV (40) + III (46) + IV (54) + IV (62) + IV (70) + IV (78) + IV (86) + IV (93-1) + IV (101) + IV (109) + IV (117) + IV (125) + IV (133) + III (139). The foliation of the 133 folios is in Roman numerals, while the last six folios are unnumbered. The manuscript is largely guillotined, so that three sections can be differentiated when establishing the dimensions of the writing box. These correspond to the internal arrangement parts of the manuscript: in the cycles of time, saints, common and vesperal (ff. 1r - 133v), with the dimensions of the writing box 158 x 102 mm; in the litany of saints (ff. 134r - 138r), with the dimensions 158 x 100 mm; and in the section of additions (ff. 138v - 139r), with the dimensions 171 x 106 mm. Arrangement of the writing: Linear layout with mainly six lines per page, except for the texts of the litanies of the saints, where the number of lines varies. Condition: Good, except for the four original flyleaves, which are in por condition. Textual writing: Textual bookplate gothic script. Musical notation: Square notation in black on a tetragram in red ink, except for two pieces that were added later, not mensural. Decoration: There are three types of initials. The first is a musical-textual line, coloured in red or blue ink; it begins each piece. The second is of a broken type, in black ink; they function as the first letter of the internal parts of each piece. The third type has a tertiary structural function, in red or blue ink. They are of the square type and appear as initials of verses and initials in litanies. This arrangement is similar to the Brussels Codex (B-Bru IV/ 473). Dating: 15th century, in any case later than the same twin processional kept in Brussels; responsorial processional, table IV in Michel Huglo, Les manuscrits du processional (p. 48*). Descripción física: 139 ff.; Formato rectangular y orientado en vertical con las dimensiones 225 x 155 x 55 mm. Escrito sobre pergamino el manuscrito ha sido encuadernado en 18 fascículos con el siguiente esquema de cuadernillos: IV (8) + IV (16) + IV (24) + IV (32) + IV (40) + III (46) + IV (54) + IV (62) + IV (70) + IV (78) + IV (86) + IV (93-1) + IV (101) + IV (109) +IV (117) + IV (125) + IV (133) + III (139). La foliación de los ciento treinta y tres folios se presenta con números romanos, mientras que los últimos seis folios no se encuentran numerados. El manuscrito está en su gran mayoría guillotinado, debido a esto se pueden diferencias tres secciones en el momento de establecer las dimensiones de la caja de escritura. Estas concuerdan con las partes de ordenación interna del manuscrito: en los ciclos del tiempo, de los santos, común y vesperal (ff. 1r – 133v), con las medidas de la caja de escritura 158 x 102 mm; en la letanía de los santos (ff. 134r – 138r), con las dimensiones 158 x 100 mm; y en la sección de adiciones (ff. 138v – 139r), con las dimensiones 171 x 106 mm. Disposición de la escritura: Línea tirada contando principalmente con seis pautados por página, exceptuando a los textos de las letanías de los santos donde el número de líneas varía. Estado de conservación: Bueno, excepto los cuatro folios originales de guarda, cuyo estado es defectuoso. Escritura textual: Letra gótica textual libraria. Notación musical: Notación cuadrada en negro sobre un tetragrama en tinta roja, excepto dos piezas que fueron añadidas posteriormente, no mensural. Decoración: Presenta tres tipos de iniciales. El primero ocupa una línea músico-textual, coloreada en tinta roja o azul; da comienzo a cada pieza. El segundo es de tipo quebrado, en tinta de color negro; funcionan como primera letra de las partes internas de cada pieza. El tercer tipo tienen función estructural terciaria, en tinta de color rojo o azul. Son de tipo cuadrado y aparecen como iniciales de los versículos e iniciales en las letanías. Esta disposición se asemeja al códice de Bruselas (B-Bru IV/ 473). Datación: Siglo XV, en todo caso posterior al igual procesional gemelo guardado Bruselas; procesional responsorial, tabla IV de Michel Huglo, Les manuscrits du processional (p. 48*).

title: E-VI (Vic) Mss. 113-114
description: Physical description: 2 volumes., 137 + 134 ff.: parchment. 470 x 340 mm. Old foliation with Roman numerals in the upper left-hand margin of the verso of ms. 113 (when the trimming of the folios allows it to be visible). Old foliation with Arabic numerals in the upper right-hand margin of the recto of ms. 113. and ms. 114. In ms. 114 there are two Arabic foliations that coincide until f. 39, from f. 40 onwards there is a difference of ten numbers for no apparent reason, as ff. 39 and 40 are contiguous. Ff. 10 and 135 of ms. 113 are missing. Moreover, there is a mismatch in the binding of some folios of ms. 113: after f. 50, f. 51 is missing, skipping directly to 52. The missing folio does appear later on, numbered as f. 61. This creates confusion in the space between folios 60 and 64 with incorrect numbering, which should be as follows:     - F. 60 is numbered correctly.     - F. 61 should really be numbered as 51, it is bound in the wrong place.     - F. 62 should be f. 61.     - F. 63 should be f. 62.     - F. 63 bis should be f. 63.     - F. 64 is numbered correctly.     This has been verified by comparing it to the Roman enumeration that can be seen in some folios.     In ms. 114 there are three intercalated folios that are unrelated to the preceding and following ones: folios 73, 80 and 113bis. In the case of f. 80, there are mismatches in the Arabic enumeration:     - F. 78 is numbered correctly.     - F. 79 does not exist.     - F. 80 is an intercalated folio that has no relation to the office on f. 78.     - F. 81 is the proper continuation of f. 78.     Ms. 113 as well as ms. 114 have a high number of scraped parts and modifications in the text and rubrics.     Musical notation: Square on four staffs, one red, one yellow and two drypoint. F and C clefs with a custos.     Content summary: The first volume contains the Proper of Time, whereas the second volume contains the Proper of Saints.                 Descripción física: 2 vols., 137 + 134 ff.: pergamino. 470 x 340 mm. Foliación antigua con numeración romana en el margen superior izquierdo del verso del ms. 113 (cuando es visible debido al recorte de los folios). Foliación antigua con numeración arábiga en el margen superior derecho del recto del ms. 113. Foliación antigua con numeración arábiga en el margen superior derecho del recto del ms. 114; en éste existen dos foliaciones arábigas coincidentes hasta el folio 39 y con un desfase de 10 a partir del f. 40 sin ninguna razón aparente, puesto que los ff. 39 y 40 van seguidos. Faltan los ff. 10 y 135 del ms. 113. Por otra parte hay un desajuste en la encuadernación de algunos folios del ms. 113: después del f. 50 falta el f. 51, pasando directamente al 52. El folio extraviado realmente aparece más adelante, numerado como f. 61. Esto hace que, entre los folios 60 y 64 haya cierta confusión, con numeraciones desajustadas que deberían ir del siguiente modo:     - El f. 60 está numerado correctamente.     - El f. 61 realmente debería ser el que aparece numerado como 51, está encuadernado fuera de sitio.     - El f. 62 debería ser f. 61.     - El f. 63 debería ser f. 62.     - El f. 63 bis debería ser f. 63.     - El f. 64 está numerado correctamente.     Todo esto se confirma cotejando con la numeración romana que se puede apreciar en algunos folios.     En el ms. 114 hay tres folios intercalados que no guardan relación con los anteriores y posteriores: los folios 73, 80 y 113bis. A propósito del f. 80, hay desajustes en la numeración arábiga relacionada con el mismo:     - El f. 78 está numerado correctamente.     - El f. 79 no existe.     - El f. 80 es un folio intercalado ajeno al oficio del f. 78.     - El f. 81 es la continuación real del f. 78.     Tanto el ms. 113 como el 114 cuentan con una gran cantidad de raspados y modificaciones en cuanto a textos y rúbricas.     Notación musical: Cuadrada sobre cuatro pautas, una roja, otra amarilla y dos en punta seca. Claves de Fa y Do con guion final.     Resumen del contenido: Contiene, en el primer volumen, el Propio del tiempo, mientras que en el segundo se encuentra el Propio de los santos.

title: E-ZAahp Archivo Histórico Provincial de Zamora 199
description: This fragment is one of a group of three that appear to have once belonged to a single source. The fragments are E-ZAahp 196, 199 and 200. Each is a bifolium. This group of fragments is referred to as 'Book A' or 'Zamora A' in Nelson (1996 and 2004-05).   Fragments 196 and 199 must have belonged to the same gathering, in which bifolium 196 was placed immediately above bifolium199: the content of side Av of 199 continues on196 side Ar, and 196 Bv continues on 199 Br. The centre of the gathering is lost.  Each of these fragments was re-used as a book cover in the binding of protocol documents from the town of Toro dating from mid-sixteenth century. The protocol books are now part of the collection of the Archivo Histórico Provincial de Zamora. Information about the protocol books was written on the outside of their parchment binding, particularly on the spine and front cover of the books. The sides which faced outwards naturally suffered the most damage, while the inward facing sides are in generally good condition.  The pictures were supplied on request by the Archive.

title: E-Pap (Palma) Cantoral 3
description: Descripción física: 132 folios, 620 × 367 mm, pergamino. Encuadernación original con cubiertas de madera y vestigios de cuero, unidas mediante un lomo de cuero y tachuelas, con restos de un cierre metálico y elementos decorativos metálicos en la cubierta. En el interior de la cubierta anterior se conservan fragmentos de papel sobre pergamino con música en notación cuadrada en tinta negra sobre pentagrama negro, que funcionan como hojas de guarda de origen más tardío.  Estado del códice: Códice mutilado debido a la pérdida de varios folios tanto en el cuerpo del volumen como al final. Presenta foliación en tinta negra en los márgenes superiores derechos del vuelto de los folios. Se observan abundantes marcas de uso.  Decoración: Iniciales de los responsorios en colores azul y rojo alternados, con adornos caligráficos; texto y notación musical en tinta negra; epígrafes y rúbricas en tinta roja.  Notación musical: Notación cuadrada en tinta negra sobre tetragrama rojo.  Resumen del contenido: Cantos de la Misa ordenados según el Propio, desde el Nominis Jesu hasta el domingo XXIV post Pentecosten, que queda incompleto.  Estado de conservación: Las cubiertas (y las hojas de guarda) están parcialmente carcomidas y desgastadas. El cuerpo del manuscrito presenta un grado considerable de deterioro debido a mutilaciones, corrosión de la tinta, fragmentos borrados, carcoma, marcas de sustancias químicas (cola) y algún palimpsesto, aunque en su mayor parte se conserva legible.

description: The fragment is difficult to date. The script suggests the fifteenth century or later; there is also significant marginal decoration in a somewhat Baroque style. (There is some evidence that antiquarian, medieval style scripts were still in use in northern Italy as late as the 1730's; see for example https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/473907) Acquired at an outdoor market in Florence, Italy. Physical description: 135 ff.: parchment; 256 x 173 mm (Anglés / Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini); 255 x 175 mm (Zauner); 260 x 180 mm (online catalogue of the Biblioteca de Catalunya). Old foliation with Roman numerals in black ink in the upper left-hand margin of the verso. Remains of modern foliation with Arabic numerals in the upper right-hand margin of the recto. A single hand is detected in ff. 1-127 and several hands in the later additions. Binding with boards covered with brown leather.     Layout of the script: nine lines of text and music in a single column.     State of conservation: excellent condition.     Decoration: capitals decorated in red, green or both.     Musical notation:     Square on a red staff. F and C clefs and a custos.     Content summary: chants for the Proper of Time (ff. 1-101r) followed by the Proper of Saints (ff. 101r-126v). There is an addition from the fourteenth century with part of the Kyrie, Gloria, Sanctus and Agnus Dei No. XV (f. 127). An addition from the fifteenth century with the Proper of the feast of Corpus Christi (f. 129). And an addition from the seventeenth century with various antiphons in white square notation (ff. 134v-135).                 Signatura: M 889.     Datación: siglo XIII ex. (Anglés / Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini); siglo XIII ex. - siglo XIV in. (Garrigosa / Zauner).     Descripción física: 135 ff.: pergamino; 256 x 173 mm (Anglés / Fdez. de la Cuesta / Janini); 255 x 175 mm (Zauner); 260 x 180 mm (Catálogo on-line de la Biblioteca de Catalunya). Foliación antigua con numeración romana a tinta negra en el margen superior izquierdo del verso. Restos de foliación moderna con numeración arábiga en el margen superior derecho del recto. Se detecta una única mano en los ff. 1-127 y varias manos en los añadidos posteriores. Encuadernación en piel marrón sobre tabla.     Disposición de la escritura: 9 líneas de texto y música a línea tirada.     Estado de conservación: Muy buena conservación.     Decoración: Capitales adornadas en rojo, verde o ambos.     Notación musical:     Notación cuadrada sobre tetragrama rojo. Claves de fa y do y guion final.     Resumen del contenido: Cantos del Propio del Tiempo (ff. 1-101r) seguido del Propio de los Santos (ff. 101r-126v). Añadido del siglo XIV con parte del Kyrie, Gloria, Sanctus y Agnus Dei nº XV (f. 127). Añadido del siglo XV con el Propio de la festividad del Corpus Christi (f. 129). title: E-PAMan (Pamplona) partitura n. 10 olim 1/11
description: A single folio measuring 295 x 218 mm (Peñas García) extracted from a breviary. Good-quality parchment with dimensions that appear to be unaltered since its copying. The state of preservation is relatively good, despite some pen tests, ink bleed-through, and damp stains. It does not have any gaps. On the reverse side of the bottom margin of the recto, one can read the word Proceso in modern handwriting, indicating that the folio was likely used as the cover of a booklet containing legal proceedings. Text in a single column with 22 lines of text and music on both sides. Gothic script, using red for the capital letters at the beginning of sections, rubrics, and guide lines, and dark black ink for everything else, always without ornamentation. Aquitaine notation in black on dry point without a key. The dots are small in size, although the pen is clearly beveled. The musical notation includes a cornuted virga, quilisma, some liquescences, and custos. Summary of the content: chants for the offices of Ursula (without a rubric, but deduced from a memorial of St. Hilary, with whom she shares the day), Crispin and Crispinian, and All Saints. In the lower margin of 1v, the verbeta 'In tempore atque tibi alme' with the prosa rubric has been copied. The verbetas are responsory proses specific to the region of Catalonia. In addition to this chant, there is a unicum for which we only have the incipit, Martyres Christi inter. Un único folio de 295 x 218 mm (Peñas García) extraído de un breviario. Pergamino de buena calidad cuyas dimensiones, aparentemente, no han sido modificadas desde su copia. El estado de conservación es relativamente bueno, a pesar de algunas pruebas de pluma, traspasos de tinta y manchas de humedad. No presenta lagunas. En el margen inferior del recto, al revés, se puede leer Proceso en letra moderna, por lo que seguramente el folio se utilizara como tapa del cuadernillo de un acta procesal. Texto a una sola columna con 22 líneas de texto y música en ambos lados. Escritura gótica, empleando rojo para las letras capitales de principio de sección, las rúbricas y las líneas de guía, y tinta negro de humo para todo lo demás, siempre sin ornamentación.  Notación aquitana en negro sobre punta seca sin clave. Los puntos son de pequeño tamaño, aunque la pluma ya está claramente cortada a bisel. La notación musical incluye virga cornuta, quilisma, algunas licuescencias y custos. Resumen del contenido: cantos de los oficios de Úrsula (sin rúbrica, pero deducido de un memorial de San Hilarión, con quien comparte día), Crispín y Crispiniano y Todos los Santos. En el margen inferior de 1v se ha copiado la verbeta In tempore atque tibi alme con la rúbrica de prosa. Las verbetas son prosas de responsorios de maitines endémicas de Cataluña. Además de este canto, destaca un unicum del que sólo tenemos el íncipit, Martyres Christi inter.

E-Sco (Sevilla) Institución Colombina Libro 063
description: This manuscript has been updated in the last quarter of the 16th century according to the Tridentine reform. Following the humanistic principles promoted by Trent, the melodies were slightly modified, although generally keeping the main design of the original versions, still visible beneath the erasures and modifications. The setting of the liturgical elements was also forcibly modified; in this case, however, it is quite impossible to see the original layer. Therefore, for the entry Use above, we indicate Roman (post-Tridentine), and in Tradition, Seville (modified according to Roman use).  Front paste-down consists of two fragmentary bifolia from a noted Breviary (15th century), with the Office of the Nativity of Mary. Rear paste-down consists of a fragment, from a Gradual (16th century), with part of the 2nd mode Alleluia Dies sanctificatus illuxit nobis.

title: E-Bbc (Barcelona) M 784
description: Shelf-mark: M 784.     Date: sixteenth century.     Physical description: 162 ff.: parchment; 585 x 395 mm (Zauner); 590 x 400 mm (online catalogue of the Biblioteca de Catalunya). Mutilated codex. Old foliation with Roman numerals in red ink in the center of the upper margin of the recto (ff. I-VIII, XI-XIV, CXXV-CXXXIII and CLXXVI are missing). There is an error in the foliation, the folio after f. LXXVI has the same number. It is the work of a single main scribe. Brown leather binding on wood with metal clasps.     Layout of the script: 8 lines of text and music in a single column.     Decoration: large number of profusely embellished capitals in alternating red and blue colours.     Musical notation: square on a red staff. F and C clefs and a custos.     Content summary: Chants for the Mass corresponding to the Proper of Time. Some folios show corrections in the text (ff. 21r, 82v, 90r, 162v, 173r, etc.) or in the music (ff. 29r, 36r, 39v-40r, etc.) that seem to respond to the adaptation of the manuscript to the criteria of the Tridentine reform.                 Signatura: M 784.     Datación: siglo XVI.     Descripción física: 162 ff.: pergamino; 585 x 395 mm (Zauner); 590 x 400 mm (Catálogo on-line de la Biblioteca de Catalunya). Códice mútilo. Foliación antigua con numeración romana a tinta roja en el centro del margen superior del recto (faltan los ff. I-VIII, XI-XIV, CXXV-CXXXIII y CLXXVI). Hay un error en la foliación, el folio siguiente al f. LXXVI tiene el mismo número. Obra de un copista principal. Encuadernación en piel marrón sobre madera con cierres metálicos.     Disposición de la escritura: 8 líneas de texto y música a línea tirada.     Decoración: Gran número de capitales profusamente adornadas y alternadas en colores rojo y azul.     Notación musical: Notación cuadrada sobre pentagrama rojo. Claves de fa y do y guion final.     Resumen del contenido: Cantos de la Misa correspondientes al Propio del tiempo. Algunos folios presentan correcciones textuales (ff. 21r, 82v, 90r, 162v, 173r, etc.) o musicales (ff. 29r, 36r, 39v-40r, etc.) que parecen responder a la adecuación del manuscrito a los criterios de la reforma tridentina.

title: E-Zs (Zaragoza) 30-116
description: Physical description: 49 ff.; Rectangular format and vertical orientation with the dimensions 255 x 290 mm. The folio size is 243 x 174 mm. Written on parchment, the manuscript has been bound in eight fascicules with the following scheme of booklets: IV (8) + IV (16) + II (19-1) + III (24-1) + IV (33+1) III (39) + II (41-2) + IV (49). The last booklet appears to have been written by another hand. Foliation in red Roman numerals. Three sections corresponding to the measurements of the writing box and the staves per page: ff. 1 - 20, five staves (Palm Sunday), ff. 21 - 41, four staves and ff. 42 - 49 (Mandatum and Holy Saturday), four staves (Purification). Original leather binding on panel (16th century). It has two folios cut in the form of tabs that have been glued to the previous back cover. Arrangement of the writing: Long line with four and five staves (staves and text) per page, except in the texts of the litanies of the saints and the rubrics, where there is a different number of lines of text per page. State of conservation: It is in good condition. Textual script: Bookplate Gothic script. Musical notation: Square notation, except for some chant sections with mensural notation (ff. 5v - 6v and 21 - 41), which correspond to a Sanctus and psalmody sections. Decoration: There are two types of initials. The first is a musical-textual line, coloured in red or blue ink; it begins each piece. The second is of a broken type, in black ink; they function as the first letter of the internal parts of some pieces. Dating: The manuscript can be dated by palaeographical estimation to the 16th century, something that would confirm the rest of the codicological and notational elements, as well as its binding. However, the manuscript itself does not provide any specific information beyond the annotation of a name. Taking into account the arrangement, we can say that it is a Roman-Franciscan processional, category IX of Michel Huglo, Les manuscrits du processional (p. 54*). Descripción física: 49 ff.; Formato rectangular y orientación vertical con las dimensiones 255 x 290 mm. La dimensión del folio es 243 x 174 mm. Escrito sobre pergamino el manuscrito ha sido encuadernado en 8 fascículos con el siguiente esquema de cuadernillos: IV (8) + IV (16) + II (19-1) + III (24-1) + IV (33+1) III (39) + II (41-2) + IV (49). El último cuadernillo parece haber sido escrito por otra mano. Foliación en números romanos de color rojo. Tres secciones correspondiendo a las medidas de la caja de escritura y a los pentagramas por página: ff. 1 -20, cinco pentagramas (Domingo de Ramos), ff. 21 – 41, cuatro pentagramas y ff. 42 – 49 (Mandatum y Sábado Santo), cuatro pentagramas (Purificación). Encuadernación original de piel sobre tabla (siglo XVI). Presenta dos folios cortados en forma de pestaña que han sido pegados en la contratapa anterior. Disposición de la escritura: Línea tirada contando con cuatro y cinco pautados (pentagramas y texto) por página, exceptuando en los textos de las letanías de los santos y las rúbricas, donde presenta un número diferente de líneas de texto por página. Estado de conservación: En buen estado. Escritura textual: Letra gótica libraria. Notación musical: Notación cuadrada, excepto algunas secciones de canto con notación mensural (ff. 5v – 6v y 21 – 41), que corresponde con un Sanctus y secciones de salmodia. Decoración: Presenta dos tipos de iniciales. El primero ocupa una línea músico-textual, coloreada en tinta roja o azul; da comienzo a cada pieza. El segundo es de tipo quebrado, en tinta de color negro; funcionan como primera letra de las partes internas de algunas piezas. Datación: El manuscrito se puede datar por estimación paleográfica del siglo XVI, algo que confirmaría el resto de los elementos codicológicos y notacionales, así como su encuadernación. No obstante, el mismo manuscrito no ofrece información específica al respecto más allá de la anotación de un nombre. Teniendo en cuenta la ordenación se puede concretar que es un procesional romano-franciscano, categoría IX de Michel Huglo, Les manuscrits du processional (p. 54*).

title: E-Zs (Zaragoza) 30-117
description: Physical description, 61 ff: This is a copy of the processional E-Zs 30-116. It is rectangular in shape and oriented vertically, with dimensions 250 x 175 mm. Written on parchment, it consists of nine fascicles: IV (8) + III (14) + III (20) + IV (28) + IV (36) + III (42) + IV (50) + V (60) + II (63-1). The dimensions of the folio and the writing box are 236 x 165 and 205 x 135 mm, respectively. Arrangement of the writing: Written in long lines. There are mostly four staves per page, with their respective text, on a grid of 28 line for writing. In the section on the litanies (ff. 56r-61v), on the other hand, the layout is arranged to fit 19 lines of text. State of conservation: In good condition. Textual script: Bookplate Gothic script. Musical notation: Square notation, some sections are notable for some mensuration (ff. 38r - 49v) and other mensural parts (ff. 50r - 54r, 56r - 61r). Decoration: Three types of initials: the first type are coloured in red at the beginning of each piece, the second type in black and correspond to the first letter of each verse of the responsories or antiphons, and the third type corresponds to the initials of the psalms and verses of the Ad Mandatum antiphons, as well as to the beginning of the deprecations and petitions of the litanies. Significantly, we find two initials illuminated with vegetal motifs (f. 1r and f. 9r). Dating: It is thought that the manuscript can be dated to the end of the 16th century on the basis of codicological and notational elements, as it does not provide specific information. In any case, this processional is later than 30-116, from which it was copied. Descripción física, 61 ff.: Es una copia del procesional E-Zs 30-116. Presenta una forma rectangular y orientado en vertical, con las dimensiones 250 x 175 mm. Escrito sobre pergamino, consta de nueve fascículos: IV (8) + III (14) + III (20) + IV (28) + IV (36) + III (42) + IV (50) + V (60) + II (63-1). Las dimensiones del folio y de la caja de escritura son 236 x 165 y 205 x 135 mm, respectivamente. Disposición de la escritura: Escrito a renglón tendido. Mayoritariamente presente cuatro pentagramas por página, con su respectivo texto, sobre un pautado de 28 líneas rectoras. En cambio, en la sección de las letanías (ff. 56r – 61v) el pautado se ha dispuesto para encajar 19 líneas de texto. Estado de conservación: En buen estado. Escritura textual: Letra gótica libraria. Notación musical: Notación cuadrada, destacan algunas secciones por encontrarse cierta mensuración (ff. 38r – 49v) y otras partes mensurales (ff. 50r – 54r, 56r – 61r). Decoración: Tres tipos de iniciales: Las del primer tipo están coloreadas en color rojo al comienzo de cada pieza, el segundo tipo en negro y corresponden con la primera letra de cada versículo de responsorios o antífonas, y el tercer tipo corresponde con las iniciales de los salmos y versículos de las antífonas Ad Mandatum, así como para iniciar las deprecaciones y peticiones de las letanías. De forma significativa, encontramos dos iniciales iluminadas con motivos vegetales (f. 1r y f. 9r). Datación: Se estima que el manuscrito se pueda datar a finales del siglo XVI teniendo en cuenta los elementos codicológicos y notacionales, ya que no el mismo no ofrece información específica. En cualquier caso, este procesional es posterior al 30-116, del cual se copió.

title: E-ZAahp Archivo Histórico Provincial de Zamora 196
description: This fragment is one of a group of three that appear to have once belonged to a single source. The fragments are E-ZAahp 196, 199 and 200. Each is a bifolium. This group of fragments is referred to as 'Book A' or 'Zamora A' in Nelson (1996 and 2004-05).   Fragments 196 and 199 must have belonged to the same gathering, in which bifolium 196 was placed immediately above bifolium199: the content of side Av of 199 continues on196 side Ar, and 196 Bv continues on 199 Br. The centre of the gathering is lost.  Each of these fragments was re-used as a book cover in the binding of protocol documents from the town of Toro dating from mid-sixteenth century. The protocol books are now part of the collection of the Archivo Histórico Provincial de Zamora. Information about the protocol books was written on the outside of their parchment binding, particularly on the spine and front cover of the books. The sides which faced outwards naturally suffered the most damage, while the inward facing sides are in generally good condition.  The pictures were supplied on request by the Archive.

title: P-Cug (Coimbra) Biblioteca Geral da Universidade MM 1063 (77)
description: This is a rare example of a manuscript with Franciscan content copied with Aquitanian neumes (of the Portuguese variety), a notational translation of the original; since the Office of St. Clare dates from the final years of the 13th century, it was probably made not long after as a supplement to a preexisting antiphoner. The fact that it does not use square notation on staff precludes its origin in a male Franciscan convent; it may have been written by a chaplain trained in a secular religious environment and attached to, or working for a female convent. The most likely candidate is the Convent of Saint Clare in Coimbra, founded in 1283 by Dona Mor Dias and re-founded in 1314 by the Queen consort Elizabeth.

title: Montréal, McGill University - Rare Books and Special Collections - Manuscript Collection, MS Medieval 0172
description: From the McGill library's description: Two separate leaves. On vellum, in latin, late 15th century gothic characters. Northern Italian (?); both leaves from the same manuscript. One column, dark-brown ink, red rubrics, red capitals and initials. Also three calligraphic initials in dark-brown ink, on the staves. Five-line staves in red with musical notation. 17-line text on 172/1r., the rest occupied by staves. 345x240 mm., writing surface 250x165 mm.Provenance unknown; not in De Ricci.  Although described by the library as Northern Italian, the rounded Praescissa hand, black/brown linework initials,  and five-line red staff may point to an Iberian origin instead. Somewhat distinctive h, with a curl descending below the text line.1v, which is all text, has 17 lines, but folios with music do not follow this ruling. 1r has six staves; on pages with mixed text and music, the staff occupies approximately three text lines. Square notation with somewhat unevenly angled clefs; thin lines of division, which are sometimes doubled or tripled; custodes pointing upward at a sharp angle; f clef with three lozenges, two of which have a small wing.

title: E-PAMan (Pamplona) partitura n. 03 olim 1/4
description: A single folio measuring 219 x 187 mm (Peñas García) extracted from an antiphonary. Dark parchment of good quality, mutilated on all four margins; the musical notation has been cut off from the top margin. The folio shows signs of having been folded. Some added texts and previous pen tests are visible in certain margins prior to the current trimming. It has two signatures: one on the recto side c-partitura, n.3 and another on the verso side, 1/4. Text in a single column, with 13 lines of text and music on both sides. Gothic script, alternating red and blue for the capital letters at the beginning of section chants (magnificat, invitatory, first responsory), and black for the rest, always without ornamentation. Rubrics and guide line in red, and the main body of text in very dark black that could be mistaken for gallow's iron ink. Aquitaine notation in black using dry-point without a clef. The dots are small in size, although the pen is clearly beveled. The musical notation includes a cornuted virga, quilisma, some liquescences, and custos. Summary of the content: antiphons from the end of the first Saturday of Lent and the beginning of the second Sunday of Lent. The six responsories contained in the fragment are not divided into nocturnes, so we cannot determine whether it is a monastic or cathedral cursus. Un único folio de 219 x 187 mm (Peñas García) extraído de un antifonario. Pergamino oscuro, de buena calidad, mutilado en los cuatro márgenes; en el margen superior se ha cercenado la notación musical. El folo presenta signos de haber permanecido doblado. En algunos márgenes se observan textos añadidos y pruebas de plumas anteriores al guillotinado actual. Presenta dos signaturas: una en el recto c-partitura, n.3 y otra en el verso, 1/4. Texto a una sola columna, con 13 líneas de texto y música en ambos lados. Escritura gótica, alternando rojo y azul para las letras capitales de los cantos de principio de sección (magníficat, invitatorio, primer responsorio) y negro para las demás, siempre sin ornamentación. Rúbricas y línea de guía en rojo y cuerpo de texto en negro muy oscuro que se podría confundir con hierro gálico. Notación aquitana en negro sobre punta seca sin clave. Los puntos son de pequeño tamaño, aunque la pluma ya está claramente cortada a bisel. La notación musical incluye virga cornuta, quilisma, algunas licuescencias y custos. Resumen del contenido: antífonas del final del primer sábado de cuaresma y principio del segundo domingo de cuaresma. Los seis responsorios que contiene el fragmento no están divididos en nocturnos, por lo que no podemos saber si se trata de cursus monástico o catedralicio. Otras observaciones: en su ficha, Peñas García intercambia verso y recto.

title: P-Cua (Coimbra) Arquivo Distrital e da Universidade IV-3ª Gav. 44 (11)
provenance: Igreja de S. Salvador de Pereiras
description: Other sources in the Cantus Database do not index the chants reported here as pertaining to Transfiguratio Domini, rather to one of the three other feasts mentioned. The two major notated Braga sources in which the feast also appears (P-BRs Ms. 28 and Ms. 34) share only a few chants with this fragment. Later, 16th c. text-only breviaries from Braga and Évora do have the same order of chants, although paired with different Matins readings. Such evidence hints at a complex net of liturgical interrelations.   The late inscriptions (see above) allow to cautiously localize the fragment as being held at a certain point either in the zone of Barcelos, some twenty kilometers West of Braga, or in Braga, whose See superintended the parish of São Salvador de Pereira. More in-depth analysis might ascertain whether it was also originally produced in the area.

title: E-PAMan (Pamplona) partitura n. 13 olim 1/14
description: A single folio measuring 200 x 270 mm (Peñas García) extracted from an antiphonary. It has been trimmed at the bottom, significantly affecting the content. The parchment is of acceptable quality, very dark, and with pores on the verso. The state of preservation is relatively good, with some moisture stains that do not hinder the reading of the content. It bears three signatures: 'c-partitura, n. 13' in the lower right margin of the recto; '1/14' in the upper right corner of the verso; and 'Nº3' in the left margin of the same side. Text in a single column. The number of lines cannot be determined due to the significant trimming of the folio at the bottom. The script is Gothic, with red and blue ink for initials and dark black ink for everything else. The initials, especially the one for the first responsory of Matins, are extensively decorated with filigree. The notation is Aquitaine on a red line, without clefs. The dots are fully square, and custos, cornuted virga, liquescences, and quilismas can be observed. Summary of the content: chants for the Common of Apostles. The antiphon of the Magnificat, 'Cum dixerint omne malum,' is noteworthy and uncommon, with concordances found in the Toledo manuscripts E-Tc 44.1 and E-Tc 44.2. Un único folio de 200 x 270 mm (Peñas García) extraído de un antifonario. Ha sido recortado en la parte inferior, afectando sensiblemente al contenido. Parche de calidad aceptable, muy oscuro y con poro en el vuelto. El estado de conservación es relativamente bueno, con algunas machas de humedad que no obstaculizan la lectura del contenido. Presenta tres signaturas: c-partitura, n. 13 en el margen inferior derecho del recto; 1/14 en la esquina superior derecha del vuelto; y Nº3 en el margen izquierdo de la misma cara. Texto a una sola columna. No podemos definir el número de líneas por el importante recorte del folio en su parte inferior. La escritura es gótica con tintas roja y azul para las iniciales y negro oscuro para lo demás. Las iniciales, especialmente la del primer responsorio de Maitines, están profusamente decoradas con filigrana. La notación es aquitana sobre una línea encarnada, sin claves. Los puntos son ya plenamente cuadrados, y se aprecian custos, virga cornuta, licuescencias y quilismae. Resumen del contenido: cantos para el Común de Apóstoles. Destaca la antífona del Magníficat, Cum dixerint omne malum, infrecuente, de la que se encuentran concordancias en los manuscritos toledanos E-Tc 44.1 y E-Tc 44.2.

title: E-Lc (León) Cod. LIV
provenance: Colegiata de San Isidoro de León
description: Physical description: 186 ff.: Rectangular format and in edict with the dimensions 14cm x 20,3cm x 6cm. Written on parchment. The manuscript has been bound in 24 fascicles with the following scheme of booklets: V (9) + III (15) + IV (23) + IV (31) + I (33) + IV (41) + IV (49) + IV (57) + II (61) + IV (69) + IV (77) + IV (85) + IV (93) + IV (101) + IV (109) + IV (117) + IV (125) + III (131) + IV (139) + IV (147) + IV (155) + IV (162) + IV (170) + IV (178) + IV (186). The codex is largely guillotined, as the foliation indications are partially sectioned or missing. Below are the foliation problems that have been encountered: ff. [1-26]: Many of the folio numbers are omitted, and the few that appear are incorrect. Additionally, the folio bearing the number 26 would actually correspond to folio 27. We assign the number f. 26b to this latter folio in the index. ff. 26b-164: The manuscript presents an omission in the foliation, jumping from f. 51 to f. 56 without affecting the content. ff. 165-175: There is an omission in the foliation, jumping from f. 164 to f. 166 without affecting the content. Additionally, f. 167 has been torn out. ff. 176-191: Many of these folios have been guillotined at the outer margin, but continuity in content and folio number is observed.  The visible foliation is in red Roman numerals. Arrangement of the writing: Linear layout of five lines per page, except for the texts of the litanies of the saints, where the number of lines varies. Textual writing: It shows some damage (guillotining - ff. 1r -27r -, wear, stains), but in general it is in good condition, probably due to use. Musical notation: Square notation in black on a staff in red ink. Decoration: There are three types of initials. The first occupies a musical-textual line, coloured in red or blue ink; it begins each piece. The second is a broken type, in black ink; it functions as the first letter of the internal parts of each piece. The third type has a tertiary structural function, in red or blue ink. Dating: 15th century (Pérez Llamazares, Fernández de la Cuesta and Huglo; 16th century (Janini), as well as its twin Ms. LIV bis preserved in the same place. In accordance to the sanctorale, this processional is from the Collegiate Church of St Isidoro, in León, Spain. The position of the feasts of the Transfixion of Mary and Dedication/Consacration of the church suggests this topic datation: they are February 9 and March 6, respectively. Descripción física: 186 ff.: Formato rectangular y en edicto con las dimensiones 14cm x 20,3cm x 6cm. Escrito sobre pergamino. El manuscrito ha sido encuadernado en 24 fascículos con el siguiente esquema de cuadernillos: V (9) + III (15) + IV (23) + IV (31) + I (33) + IV (41) + IV (49) + IV (57) + II (61) + IV (69) + IV (77) + IV (85) + IV (93) + IV (101) + IV (109) + IV (117) + IV (125) + III (131) + IV (139) + IV (147) + IV (155) + IV (162) + IV (170) + IV (178) + IV (186). El códice se encuentra guillotinado en su gran mayoría, ya que las indicaciones de foliación se encuentran parcialmente seccionadas o no aparecen. A continuación se detallan los problemas de foliación que se han encontrado: ff. [1-26]: gran parte de los números de folio se omiten y los pocos que aparecen son erróneos. Además, el folio que lleva el número 26 correspondería en realidad el folio 27. Otorgamos en el índice el número f. 26b a este último folio. ff. 26b-164: el manuscrito presenta una omisión en la foliación, que salta del f. 51 al f. 56 sin afectar al contenido. ff. 165-175: la foliación presenta una omisión en la foliación, que salta del f. 164 al f. 166 sin afectar al contenido. Además, ha sido arrancado el f. 167. ff. 176-191: gran parte de estos folios han sido guillotinados en el margen externo, pero se advierte continuidad en el contenido y en el número de folio. La foliación visible es en números romanos de color rojo.  Disposición de la escritura: Línea tirada contando con cinco pautados por página, exceptuando a los textos de las letanías de los santos donde el número de líneas varía. Estado de conservación: Presenta algunos daños (guillotinados – ff. 1r -27r – , desgaste, manchas), pero en general está en buen estado, probablemente por el uso. Escritura textual: Letra gótica textual libraria. Notación musical: Notación cuadrada en negro sobre un pentagrama en tinta roja. Decoración: Presenta tres tipos de iniciales. El primero ocupa una línea músico-textual, coloreada en tinta roja o azul; da comienzo a cada pieza. El segundo es de tipo quebrado, en tinta de color negro; funcionan como primera letra de las partes internas de cada pieza. El tercer tipo tiene función estructural terciaria, en tinta de color rojo o azul. Datación: siglo XV (Pérez Llamazares, Fernández de la Cuesta y Huglo; siglo XVI (Janini), al igual que su gemelo Ms. LIV bis conservado en el mismo lugar. Resumen del contenido: Contiene responsorios, antífonas e himnos destinados a las procesiones de los domingos y las fiestas solemnes del año, según el ritual propio de la colegiata. Según se indica en el códice, la música es escrita y trasladada (ex monachorda in penthacorda) por parte de D. Lorenzo Ramos. Existen otros volúmenes procesionales con la signatura Cód. LV y Cód. LVI. De acuerdo al santoral, este procesional es de la Colegiata de San Isidoro de León. La posición de las festividades de la Transfixión de María y Dedicación/Consagración de la iglesia así lo sugiere: estas son el 9 de febrero y 6 de marzo, respectivamente.

description: The photographs included here were taken by Manuel Pedro Ferreira in the early 1990s before the disappearance of the fragment. The dating is that given by Bragança who in 1993 published a detailed study of the source (see below) including a nearly complete transcription of the textual content. Bragança demonstrates that this fragment represents the liturgy of Braga and discusses connections with the Missal of Mateus (Braga, Arquivo Distrital, MS 1000) and the Pontifical of Braga (Lisbon, BN, Alc. 162). The Carolingian script of the fragment shows marked influence of Visigothic script with frequent use of the Visigothic 't' being particularly noticeable.

description: This reconstructed parchment leaf contains four fragments that are part of a series of musical binding materials (The Ridgefield Project). (See https://cantusdatabase.org/source/714555.) title: Connecticut, Private collections, D:07lvz
description: This reconstructed parchment leaf is composed of six fragments that are part of a series of musical binding materials (The Ridgefield Project). The parchment was used to bind volumes of the Histoire Ecclesiastique pour servir de continuation à celle de Monsieur l'Abbé Fleury (Paris, Pierre-Jean Mariette, 1720-1730). (See https://cantusdatabase.org/source/714555). The parchment pieces found in the Ridgefield Project appear to be from a thirteenth-century antiphoner and gradual from an (as yet unidentified) Cistercian monastery, possibly in France or Belgium. This half folio is composed of six binding pieces (Group C) from Volumes 15, 17, and 21 of the Histoire, and is from an antiphoner. The chants are for the feast of Agatha; it is likely this folio was near Group B (perhaps even as part of a bifolio).

title: E-PAMan (Pamplona) partitura n. 11 olim 1/12
description: A single folio measuring 266 x 196 mm (Peñas García) extracted from a breviary. Good-quality parchment mutilated in the lower and outer margins. The puncture marks from the original binding can be observed in the inner margin. On the upper margin of the reverse side, one can read 'Proceso de Don Pedro de Rodicillas Ximenez y Cascante [...] del año 1687 contra don Lorenço de Azoilia [...]', indicating that this fragment was reused as the cover of a booklet containing legal proceedings. Text in two columns with approximately 22 lines of music and text on each side, although the cut in the lower part of the fragment prevents us from knowing for sure. Gothic script, alternating red and blue with filigree in the contrasting color for the capital letters, and black for everything else. Irregular strokes. Aquitaine notation on a pulled red line without a guide. Medium-sized dots with a square appearance. The musical notation includes a cornuted virga, quilisma, some liquescences, and custos. Summary of the content: responsories and antiphons for the matins of the feast of the Ascension. Un único folio de 266 x 196 mm (Peñas García) extraído de un breviario. Pergamino de buena calidad mutilado en los márgenes inferior y exterior. En el margen interior se observan las marcas de punzón del encuadernado original. En el margen superior del vuelto se puede leer Proceso de Don Pedro de Rodicillas Ximenez y Cascante [...] del año 1687 contra don Lorenço de Azoilia [...], por lo que sabemos que este fragmento se reutilizó como tapa del cuadernillo de un acta procesal. Texto a dos columnas con unas 22 líneas de música y texto a cada lado, si bien el recorte en la parte inferior del fragmento nos impide saberlo con seguridad. Escritura gótica, alternando rojo y azul con filigrana en el contrario para las letras capitales y negro para lo demás. Trazo irregular. Notación aquitana sobre una línea encarnada tirada sin guía. Puntos de tamaño medio, con apariencia cuadrada. La notación musical incluye virga cornuta, quilisma, algunas licuescencias y custos. Resumen del contenido: responsorios y antífonas de maitines de la fiesta de la Ascensión.

description: De Trinitate: complete agreement with the Évora printed breviary of 1528 (P-Ln RES. 253 P.) up until the conclusive Benedictus antiphon. From this point onward this fragment variously and inconsistently agrees with P-Br Ms 32 and the said breviary.De Regum: the rather rare responsory verses 007372b and 007510b point to a decidedly Aquitanian and Iberian tradition (the former is a unicum in Portuguese sources as of Apr. '22).Together with P-Br Ms 32 and P-Ln RES. 253 P., this source presents some minor textual variants apparently proper to Portugal to some degree. In order of appearance, see for example the responsory verse Trinitati lux, the antiphons O beata et benedicta and Rex autem David. Some divergences are still appreciable nonetheless: such is the case of the antiphon O gloriosa et beata (a possibly local antiphon particular to Iberia) which instead reads O gloriosa et benedicta in P-Ln RES. 253 P. Similarly small textual variants in other chants pertaining the Holy Trinity are documented that are  apparently local to Portugal: see for example P-Cua IV-3ª Gav. 44 (11), a fragment possibly produced in the area of Braga and roughly contemporary to the present one. Finally, as of Oct. '22 the responsory verse 006239ze is only shared with Toledo 44.2 in the Cantus database.

description: A single sheet cut at its top and outer part with current measurements of 280 x 200 (Peñas García). Good-quality parchment, with significant gaps, cuts, and moisture stains. Tinta negra para el cuerpo del texto y rojo para las rúbricas y las letras iniciales.  Notación aquitana sobre una línea a punta seca sin claves. description: Partial leaf from a noted missal, 296 x130 mm (writing area 275 x 92 mm). Text appears to be transitional Praegothica of the late 12th or early 13th century; some rubrics are in capitals and others not. Neumes are unheightened and largely of the German variety, though with a head on the virga, hooks on clives and a downward-pointing trigon rather than St Gall forms. The neumes for the mass ordinary incipits for Easter have been given in red.The fragment was used for binding, and has a fold along one side and a missing rectangle in one corner (presumably from damage where the parchment was pasted down); a few wormholes are visible in the margin. Based on the dimensions, it seems likely it is one column of a two-column leaf. Ruled for 36 lines (the lower margin is trimmed, but text is not substantially missing.) The library's previous description dated the fragment much later; both the current and previous descriptions are provided below for reference. 2018 description read:Part of one leaf containing one column of text (lower margin is missing). 36 lines on recto and 35 on verso, from which thirteen, on recto, and seven, on verso, contain musical notation. In Latin, on vellum. Probably written in the 15th century, gothic characters, unknown origin. 296x130 mm.; written surface 275x092 mm. Wormholed, large hole on upper part of fragment. Probably used for binding. Brown ink, red rubrics, one and two-line initials in red ink.  From Sabbato sancto. r. in quo non est iniquitas iustus et sanctus Dominus (with musical notation). Followed by orationes, Paul's Ad Colossenses (Col. 3) and Matthew's: Vespere autem Sabbati quae (Mat. 28) lucescit in prima Sabbati venit v. Maria Magdalene et altera Maria videre Populus acquisitionis annunciate virtute eius quivos de tenebris vocatur. (Holland, Anne Marie, compiler. MS Medieval 176. Long Descriptions Ms Medieval Manuscript Antiphonals, Missals and Graduals. Digitization and Cataloguing Project- Antiphonals, Missals and Gradual. Updated December 6, 2018), 22-23. Revised description in McGill's online catalogue reads (as of 2025): One damaged vellum leaf from a late 12th-century noted missal written in Germany ; texts and musical notation (staffless German neumes) in brown ink ; liturgical rubrics in red ink ; single line and two-line initials in red ; faded marginal annotations in red on verso. Damage includes missing music and text due to abraded edges and the loss of a narrow rectangular hole extending down from the top edge Mass texts and chants for Sancto Sabbato. https://mcgill.on.worldcat.org/oclc/1303698559
